emcees.name: 2khelle
emcees.bio: If there's an award for the most hated emcee in FlipTop, it would definitely go to 2khelle. The rapper from Olongapo angered battle rap fans from all over the country after a highly controversial win over BLKD at the Gapo De Gulat event in 2010. Since then, he quickly became the subject of various online hate comments. Instead of succumbing to the negativity, 2khelle ignored the harsh remarks and continued battling in the league. No one can deny that his stage presence and creative jokes are always effective. He may have lost against Nico at Aspakan 1, but it was the match where he proved that he's also gifted in freestyling. All you need is an open mind to fully appreciate him as a battle emcee.

emcees.name: 3rdy
emcees.bio: Davao's 3rdy first appeared at the Won Minutes Mindanao event in June 2023. Many applauded his lyricism but his battle against Negho Gy at the finals of Motus Battle League's Pedestal 2 Tournament is where he truly gained recognition. His performance was enough to get him a spot not only in Ahon 14, but also in FlipTop's roster. 3rdy took on Class G in the aforementioned event, scoring an impressive unanimous decision win. He quickly became well-known for his impressive wordplays and metaphors as well as his strong stage presence.

emcees.name: Abra
emcees.bio: Abra was already a well-known freestyler in the late 2000's, so when FlipTop was established, he immediately got a spot in its roster. He lost his debut battle, but was able to bounce back at the inaugural Bwelta Balentong event. Abra immediately turned into a fan favorite thanks to his clever jokes, impressive speedy flow, and well-constructed multi-syllabic rhymes. In 2012, he joined the Dos Por Dos Tournament with Loonie and their clash with Shehyee and Smugglaz remain to be one of the most viewed battles in FlipTop. Abra also has a successful career in music. He released his self-titled solo album in 2013, which features the hit single Gayuma.

emcees.name: Aklas
emcees.bio: Aklas was part of the very first Process of Illumination and despite not reaching the finals, his impressive freestyle skills were enough to land him a spot in the roster. On his debut match, the rapper from Las Pinas quickly made an impact with his aggressive delivery and hard-hitting lines. Some may say that he doesn't really “rhyme” in his battles, but if you listen closely, you will realize that he has an unorthodox pen game. Without a doubt, he's one of the very few emcees in FlipTop who has mastered “leftfield” style. In 2013, he joined the first Isabuhay Tournament and shocked everyone by beating crowd-favorite BLKD to become the champion. Apart from the battle scene, Aklas also remains active in music. He has independently released 5 solo albums and 1 instrumental EP, all of which you can check out online. Before venturing into Hiphop, he was the vocalist of a metal band called “NOTIME”.

emcees.name: AKT
emcees.bio: AKT, formerly known as Nico, is a FlipTop OG. He was part of the inaugural FlipTop event in Olongapo (Gapo De Gulat), taking on Sayadd. His first loss didn't stop him at all from continuing his battle rap journey. After failing to get the W again versus Damsa, he worked on improving his pen game and came back with a vengeance. Nico started collecting impressive wins from the likes of Shehyee and G-Spot. Unfortunately, some controversial results from the first Gapo De Gulat event put a bad name not only on his hometown but on himself and the rest of the emcees as well. The overwhelming hate gave way to his AKT persona. AKT immediately became well-received thanks to his highly unorthodox approach to lyricism. His delivery, which is akin to a raving madman, adds more intensity to his controversial bars. Battle rap is not the sole focus of AKT. He has released two full-length albums as well, namely “Personality in Disorder” and “Straight Outta System”. Both projects feature his uncompromising, take-no-prisoners style. AKT also has a book called “Peenoise”, which is a collection of short stories written by him. It's independently published and can be bought on Shopee.

emcees.name: Andy G
emcees.bio: Laguna's Andy G made his debut in mid 2010, and while he had an unimpressive start, he was able to bounce back quickly. His first win was against Harlem at Ahon 2, where he showed his more serious side. He then decided to mix aggression with his own brand of humor, and it eventually became his signature style. The DC Clan representative became even more well-known after a highly entertaining performance versus Malupit in December of 2013. Battle rap fans also consider his match with Fongger to be one of the funniest battles in FlipTop.

emcees.name: Antonym
emcees.bio: Antonym first became well-known for his appearance at Pilipinas Got Talent, reaching the semi-finals with his impressive spoken word performances. He then decided to give battle rap a shot, competing in leagues such as Motus and gaining a few solid wins. In February 2024, he became part of FlipTop's Won Minutes Luzon event, beating James Overman in a cerebral matchup. His big stage debut took place at the 17th edition of Zoning on the first of June. He may have lost against Negho Gy, but many still appreciated his poetic style and strong presence.

emcees.name: Apekz
emcees.bio: Apekz first appeared at the inaugural Second Sight event, where he took on Harlem in a freestyle battle. He may have lost his FlipTop debut, but he quickly made an epic comeback at Ahon 1, outrapping Snatch for three rounds. From there, Apekz continued his ascent to the top. Apart from his creative jokes, he also became famous for his intricate multis and effective “real talk” bars. Fans will certainly have different opinions about his best performance in the league, but no one can deny that his match with Badang is where he showed his versatility in battling. Apekz also achieved success in music with his solo album “Ala Una”, which was released in 2017 on Spotify.

emcees.name: Apoc
emcees.bio: Apoc was part of the inaugural Grain Assault event, and while he lost his first few battles due to chokes, he was able to bounce back at Aspakan 1 by verbally demolishing Sayantipiko. Since then, he ascended to the top and has no plans of climbing down. Apoc is one of the first in the league to utilize wordplays, metaphors, and similes, and he spits them all with confidence and aggression. He's also a threat when it comes to constructing angles. The rounds are broken down into separate topics, all of which are directly related to the opponent. This style was proved effective when he faced Smugglaz, Tipsy D, Zend Luke, and many others. When he's not battling, Apoc is busy writing songs and making beats. His debut album Loob Ng Kabaong was released in September of 2017 to critical acclaim.

emcees.name: Arma
emcees.bio: Arma started his rap career as an emcee for Gerahay Letra, an underground battle league based in Iloilo. In 2019, he was discovered by Anygma and instantly became part of FlipTop's roster. The Iloilo City emcee joined the first two Won Minutes events in Cebu, winning both battles in impressive fashion. At Unibersikulo 10, Arma joined forces with Castillo to take on Vitrum and Illtimate. They weren't able to get the W, but fans and fellow emcees still admired their performance. Arma has the ability to mix freestyle and written in his rounds while maintaining his aggressive delivery. When it comes to his pen game, he can effortlessly switch from technical to comedic and vice versa. Expect more memorable performances from him in future events.

emcees.name: Article Clipted
emcees.bio: Article Clipted's battle rap career started in Digmaan, a league based in his hometown of General Santos City. He made his first FlipTop appearance at Won Minutes 2023 Mindanao, defeating Derekta in what many consider the battle of the night. In mid 2024, he teamed up with Sickreto at the Dos Por Dos2 Tournament. They lost against Aubrey and Marichu in the first round, but their performance still gained the respect of the crowd. Article Clipted scored his next victory at Pakusganay 8, beating Dosage via unanimous decision. In 2025, he joined the Isabuhay Tournament, taking on Carlito in the first round. Despite not getting the win, many agree he gave a solid performance. He quickly became known for his flawless mix of leftield and horrorcore styles as well as his intense delivery. The Gensan emcee, apart from battle rap, remains active in making music. His debut solo LP “Pagmulat” was released on July 12, 2022, where he also produced all of the beats. He has a group with VXDZ, Classico, Driex, and Moy called 8.51G. Their album “Tumor” came out on May 27, 2017. It's available on their Soundcloud page.

emcees.name: Asser
emcees.bio: Asser started out at the Ubec Mindfields Tryouts, where he was crowned the champion. In his debut battle at Gubat 1, he proved that he truly belongs in the league. If you go one-on-one with Asser, expect him to break your rapping style down in the most creative why. He will expose all of your weaknesses using well-written multis and a fast-paced flow. What makes him special is that despite his fast way of rapping, you can still understand every word. His first battle with Rapido remains to be one of the best face-offs in FlipTop. Asser is also passionate when it comes to music. In early 2017, he independently released his solo album entitled Walang Permanente.

emcees.name: Atoms
emcees.bio: Atoms of Albay started to make an impact in the battle rap scene after giving incredible performances in Motus Battle League. His FlipTop debut took place on the 3rd of August 2024 at Won Minutes Luzon 3. He took on Caytriyu and even though he didn't get the W, fans still appreciated his solid technical lyricism and energetic presence. Atoms then teamed with Cygnus of Naga City at the 2024 Dos Por Dos Tournament. Their impeccable chemistry and flawless pen game are enough for them to win the championship at Ahon 15.

emcees.name: Aubrey
emcees.bio: Aubrey first gained recognition in leagues such as Motus and Sunugan. Her remarkable performances earned her a spot at Won Minutes 2024 2 in Metro Manila. She defeated Hempphil in dominant fashion. On the same year, she teamed up with fellow femcee Marichu for Dos Por Dos2, where they reached the semifinals. In 2025, Aubrey joined the Isabuhay Tournament. The Pandacan representative took on Lhipkram on the first round, and despite losing, she gained the respect of the FlipTop fanbase. Her hard-hitting bars, creative metaphors, and raw aggression remain her biggest strengths.

emcees.name: Bagsik
emcees.bio: After making an impact in various amateur leagues, Bagsik finally became part of FlipTop's roster in 2019. He calls himself “pinaka mabait na emcee” (the kindest emcee); a sharp contrast to his battling style. Bagsik is well-known for his in-your-face angles, which often revolve around his opponents' personal lives. Even if some are just made up, his personals are always effective thanks to his convincing delivery. Bagsik is also highly skilled in multisyllabic rhyming, often experimenting with different schemes. You can check out his solo and collaboration tracks on his YouTube channel “BAGSIK OFFICIAL”. His music, just like his battles, features his hard-hitting, confrontational style. Outside of the hip-hop scene, Bagsik is selling his very own brand of chili garlic sauce. It consistently gets rave reviews online and continues to sell really well. He also established a clothing line last year called “Asar Talo”.

emcees.name: Ban
emcees.hometown: Ibabao, Cordova, Cebu & Ibo, Lapu-Lapu City
emcees.bio: One of the special picks from Process of Illumination 7, Ban first became well-known in Visayas after becoming the CRBL Champion in 2019 and reaching the finals of RAPOLLO's Laglag Bara 5 Tournament in 2022. He made his FlipTop debut at Gubat 11 on April 14, facing fellow #POI7 special pick Empithri. After three rounds of back-and-forth action, Ban won by split decision. No one can deny the impact of his heavy lines and witty humor plus his aggressive delivery. Just like the majority of the emcees in the league, Ban also makes music. His solo EP “TAPULAN”, which contains four songs, was released in June 2022 on YouTube. Don't forget to check out his other tracks on his channel.

emcees.name: Bassilyo
emcees.bio: If you're a Pinoy rap fan, then you've probably heard of Bassilyo even before FlipTop. He and his group Crazy as Pinoy enjoyed moderate success in the early 2000's when they joined the Rap Public contest in Eat Bulaga. In 2012, he decided to give FlipTop a shot by participating at the first Dos Por Dos with his friend CrazyMix. Despite losing at the quarterfinals, their incredible chemistry and performance made them fan favorites in an instant. The duo had a better showing at the 2013 tournament, where they were able to reach the finals. As of now, Bassilyo only has one singles battle in the league (vs. Zaito), but it was enough for him to showcase his comedic style. He's also effective when it comes to serious “real talk” lines, as seen in his Dos Por Dos matches. Bassilyo's success in music is undeniable as well. His album Klasik, which was released in 2013, has been certified triple platinum.

emcees.name: Batang Rebelde
emcees.bio: Batang Rebelde made his FlipTop debut in December of 2011, scoring an impressive victory against Jonas. He then joined the first Dos Por Dos Tournament with Rapido and even though they lost the first round, the crowd still enjoyed their performance. The Tanza-based rapper continued his solo battling career, showcasing his unique blend of humor and technical bars. This style can be seen in full force in his battle versus Frooz at 2017's Zoning event. He participated in three Isabuhay Tournaments and despite never advancing from the first round, it didn't stop him from remaining active in the battle arena. Batang Rebelde is truly one of the most dedicated emcees in the league. As for his songs, most of them are available on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Batas
emcees.bio: Batas is one of the first emcees to step foot in the FlipTop stage, and his hardcore approach made him the two-time Isabuhay champion. When you go face-to-face with him, you better expect plenty of hurtful words from the first to the last round. Batas spits his venomous rhymes with an aggressive flow and delivery that will leave the viewers wanting more. He has plenty of classic battles under his belt, but the one with Dello remains to be the most well-known. It's where he was hailed as the official “bad guy” of the league. Love him or hate him, there's no denying that he introduced the Filipino fans to a more hard-hitting style of battling. You can hear more of Batas' cutthroat lyricism in his music. His group Illustrado, which includes Sayadd, Goriong Talas, and Apo Lerma, have released two full-length albums so far, both of which are under Uprising Records and received positive reviews. In December 2021, he dropped his first full-length solo LP entitled "Ginoong Rodriguez", which is also critically acclaimed.

emcees.name: Bisente
emcees.bio: Tondo's Bisente started out in Rapcapella, Sunugan Kalye, and Motus, where he was a semifinalist at the Pedestal 3 Tournament. He debuted in FlipTop on May 2024 at Won Minutes Luzon 2, defeating BLZR in a very lyrical battle. His impressive performance earned him a spot on the big stage. Bisente then faced off against Jawz at Unibersikulo 12. Despite losing the match, fans still appreciated his overall skills. Apart from his solid technical pen game, his aggressive delivery and intense presence are very effective. Bisente is also active in making music. So far in 2024, he has released one single and three music videos.

emcees.name: Blackleaf
emcees.bio: Blackleaf is a veteran in Davao's rich hip-hop scene. He and his group Lifelinez represent the leftfield style of rapping. Their music was eventually discovered by Anygma online. In 2011, Anygma decided to name Blackleaf as the president of the league's Mindanao Division. The Davao-born emcee has a few battles under his belt, all of which feature his trademark aggressive and unorthodox approach. His last match was a dominating victory against Makii in Cebu. Up to now, Blackleaf remains active in music as part of Kalawakan Krew. He has released plenty of projects, from solos to collaborations. Apart from emceeing, he's also a respected beatmaker. His instrumentals are often dark and grim, making him one of the pioneers of that sound in his hometown.

emcees.name: BLKD
emcees.bio: BLKD joined the first FlipTop tryout in 2010, and even though he wasn't able to reach the finals, his performance earned him a spot in the roster. Fast forward to the present, the Cavite-born emcee has become synonymous with “bars”. While the concept was already introduced earlier in the league, it was him who made the technical style popular among fans. He also uses the battle stage as his platform to air out his grievances to the government. BLKD will cleverly find a way to insert a socially-conscious line, without abandoning his opponent. His writing skill extended to music, and this is evident in his critically-acclaimed 2015 album with DJ UMPH entitled “Gatilyo”.

emcees.name: BLZR
emcees.bio: BLZR's battle rap career began in the underground. He started out in leagues such as Motus and FRBL. On May 2024, he made his FlipTop debut, taking on Bisente. Despite losing, many admired his lyricism and performance. BLZR scored his first victory at Unibersikulo 12, defeating Freek by unanimous decision. His latest battle in the league was against Antonym at Zoning 19 and while he may have lost, the match still gained a positive reception. He quickly became known for his calm-but-deadly delivery, wide vocabulary, and heavy punches. He returned to his underground roots in late 2024 by participating in Insane Battles' UTMOST Tournament. The Pililla emcee went home with the championship. When he's not battling, BLZR is busy with music. His solo EP “The Aftermath” come out on August 25, 2022, and you can check it out on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Bonet
emcees.bio: After making his presence known in the underground rap battle world, Bonet decided to join the Metro Manila Process of Illumination tryouts in 2018. He wasn't able to win the championship, but his superb freestyle ability still got him a spot in FlipTop's roster. For his debut match, he faced Cricket and won via unanimous decision. The emcee from Commonwealth remained active in the league, defeating Lemi and Supremo during the quarantine battles era. His hardcore lyrical style and clear delivery continue to be his biggest strengths.

emcees.name: C-Quence
emcees.bio: C-Quence is the definition of heart. He went home empty-handed at the 2018 Process of Illumination in Calabarzon, but decided to join again at the Metro Manila event where he became part of the special picks. C-Quence immediately made waves in his debut battle with a unanimous decision win over Lemi. Since then, he has been an active emcee in FlipTop. The pandemic didn't stop C-Quence from showcasing his rhyming skills. He's one of the rappers who shined during the league's quarantine battles era. The Cavite-born lyricist won his next six battles, all of which were in dominating fashion. No can deny his creative mix of serious and comedic lines as well as his flawless rebuttals. He's indeed a total package emcee.

emcees.name: Caspher
emcees.bio: Caspher has achieved legendary status in the underground battle rap scene in 2022, winning championships in three different leagues: Sin Zone, Bara sa Kalye, and Ekisan. He also made an impact in Motus, reaching the semifinals of the first and third Pedestal Tournaments. In February 2024, the rapper from Dasmarinas finally made his FlipTop debut, beating R-Zone in a solid match at Won Minutes Luzon. Caspher then took on Andros at Zoning 17 and won via unanimous decision. His incredible rhyme schemes as well as his sharp delivery and well-rounded writing make him a legit threat.

emcees.name: Castillo
emcees.bio: Castillo began his battle rap journey as an emcee for the underground league Gerahay Letra. His undeniable skills were eventually discovered by Anygma in 2019. Castillo then made his FlipTop debut at the first Won Minutes event in Cebu, beating Jahmen J via unanimous decision. In November 2021, he and fellow Ilonggo emcee Arma teamed up to face Vitrum and Illtimate in Metro Manila. They lost the battle, but they were still able to impress the viewers with their chemistry and overall performance. Castillo bounced back from his Metro Manila loss at Ahon 12 by defeating Bagsik in a heated battle. Since then, he's been considered a legitimate threat in the league. Apart from his confident stage presence, Castillo's mix of hard-hitting and funny bars is also his biggest strength.

emcees.name: Caytriyu
emcees.bio: Caytriyu entered the world of battle rap around 10 years ago, becoming an active emcee at Raplines. He was the inaugural champion of the league's Numero Uno Tournament. The Las Pinas emcee proceeded to showcase his skills at other organizations such as PULO and Sunugan Kalye. He took a 7-year break from battling then returned on January 2024, facing Anotnym in a back-and-forth classic at Motus. Caytriyu finally debuted in FlipTop at Won Minutes Luzon 2024 3, where he battled and defeated Atoms. He then went up against Tulala at Second Sight 13. Many fans in attendance consider their match the battle of the night. Caytriyu's arsenal includes clever wordplays and metaphors, hard-hitting angles, and an unpredictable delivery.

emcees.name: Cerberus
emcees.bio: In February of 2014, Cerberus drove from Pampanga to Metro Manila to join the fourth Process of Illumination. The long trip was worth it because he was able to join FlipTop's official roster. He faced Sayantipiko in his debut at Aspakan 2, and got an impressive 5-0 win. Apart from his aggressive delivery, Cerberus also became renowned for his brutal punchlines. You can see him utilize this style to the fullest in his classic battle with Lanzeta.

emcees.name: Class G
emcees.bio: Class G took the battle rap world by storm by becoming Motus Battle League's Pedestal 2022 Tournament Champion. It was enough to get him a spot in FlipTop in early 2023. Class G finally made his debut at Second Sight 11, facing off against Lax Hartis. His intense stage presence and hard-hitting bars immediately gained him a strong following. Like other battle emcees in FlipTop, Class G also aims to succeed through music. You can listen to his tracks on his YouTube page. He's just getting started, so make sure you keep an eye out for his upcoming projects.

emcees.name: CNine
emcees.bio: CNine is a well-known emcee in Bulacan's underground hip-hop scene. He then decided to join FlipTop's 2018 Process of Illumination tryouts in Pampanga. His flawless freestyle skills were showcased all throughout, ultimately leading to a championship win. CNine's debut battle took place at the inaugural Won Minutes event, where he once again faced his tryout finals opponent JDee. He got the W on his first official match, and his winning streak continued from there. CNine is one of the rappers who were active during the quarantine battles era of the league. Apart from his off-the-top abilities, his writtens have also vastly improved. He instantly became known for his unique brand of humor and unpredictable angles.

emcees.name: Cool Kidd
emcees.bio: Cool Kidd debuted in 2011 at 082 Magnitude, scoring an impressive victory against Madd NJ. Fans were treated to some awe-inspiring rhyme schemes and clever angles. From there, his pen game further improved, which led to some underrated classics against Nikki, Stiff, and Aelekz. When he's not battling, Cool Kidd does photography work for MurderCapital Clothing and makes music with his group Karabineros. He is best known for the “PERA”, a collaboration track with Malupit and Sak Maestro.

emcees.name: Crazymix
emcees.bio: Crazymix made his debut at the first Dos Por Dos with Bassilyo. Even though they took the L at the quarterfinals, their performance still clicked with battle rap fans. The duo joined once again at the 2013 tournament and was able to reach the finals. As a solo emcee, Crazymix is also a force to be reckoned with. He may have lost his first 1-on-1 battle, but after improving his pen game, he went on to win his next two. The Marikina-born emcee is known for his bars and jokes, which are delivered with a rapid fire flow. In his match against Damsa at Ahon 5, he successfully proved that he was the superior speed rapper.

emcees.name: CRhyme
emcees.bio: CRhyme initially garnered recognition in the underground battle rap scene, becoming the champion of PULO's Titulo Tournament in 2019. The Las Pinas emcee made his FlipTop debut at Won Minutes Luzon 2024 2, defeating Dodong Saypa in what many consider the most entertaining battle of the night. He then took on Supremo at Second Sight 13 and secured his second win. His most recent battle was at Zoning 18 versus Caspher. Despite losing, his performance captivated the audience. CRhyme became well-known for his creative mix of comedy and hard-hitting bars as well as his intricate rhyme schemes and strong presence. He remains active in the underground battle circuit.

emcees.name: CripLi
emcees.bio: CripLi traveled all the way from Naga to Calabarzon just to be part of the Process of Illumination 5 tryouts. His dedication paid off when he got accepted into the league's official roster. Despite losing his debut battle at Grain Assault 7, he got the respect of the crowd with his witty jokes, energetic delivery, and simple but effective technical bars. He and Towpher took on Invictus and Lanzeta at Ahon 7 and won by unanimous decision. Many claim it was the best performance of both emcees. The duo joined the Dos Por Dos Tournament in 2017 and even though they lost in the first round, FlipTop fans still lauded their performance. CripLi continues to improve his pen game, which is evident in his Zoning battle against Range and most recently, JKing.

emcees.name: Crispy Fetus
emcees.bio: The unorthodox lyrical skill and impressive discography of Crispy Fetus were enough for him to be chosen as one of the special picks at the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts in Cavite. He only has one battle in FlipTop so far, but it already gave us a glimpse of his bizarre style. The masked emcee has the ability to combine vile horrorcore bars with leftfield humor. His menacing delivery gives him a psychopathic supervillain vibe. This style can also be heard in his solo projects, the latest of which is a full-length LP entitled “Duling”. His albums and EPs are available on all streaming platforms. As for his battle career, you can expect him to return and be better than ever soon!

emcees.name: Cygnus
emcees.bio: Naga City's Cygnus began his battle rap career by making waves in leagues such as Engkwentro and Motus. His first FlipTop battle happened at Won Minutes Luzon 3, defeating Jamy Sykes in a showcase of pure lyricism. Fans in attendance admired not only his perfect mix of technical lines and humor but also his rapid-fire flow and aggressive delivery. He then joined forces with fellow Bicolano emcee Atoms at the 2024 Dos Por Dos Tournament. Thanks to their undeniable chemistry and top-tier material, they were crowned the champions at Ahon 15.

emcees.name: Daddie Joe D
emcees.bio: Daddie Joe D debuted at the first Ahon event, where he shocked everyone by beating Shehyee. His hard punchlines and swift flow were enough to destroy his opponent. He may have lost his next three bouts, but he was able to redeem himself at Ahon 2 against Damsa. It was the night when he showcased a more serious and aggressive approach to battling. Since then, Daddie Joe D decided to add his unique brand of humor to his style, which led to more notable victories.

emcees.name: Damsa
emcees.bio: There are only a few emcees in FlipTop who can flawlessly rap fast, and Damsa is one of them. While his debut at Down N South in 2010 was a bit unimpressive, he bounced back at Grain Assault 2 using his trademark flow. 2016 was arguably his greatest year thanks to his consecutive victories. If you want to witness Damsa's impressive flow in full force, then check out his Gubat 5 clash with Flict-G. He eventually teamed up with his aforementioned opponent at the Dos Por Dos Tournament in 2017, where they were able to reach the semi-finals.

emcees.name: Dave Denver
emcees.bio: Dave Denver of Baras began his battle rap career by competing in leagues such as Motus and FRBL. He finally debuted in FlipTop on the 4th of May 2024 at Won Minutes. Despite losing against Keelan, his performance earned him another shot in the league. At Second Sight 13, he bounced by beating Kalixs in an entertaining battle. The crowd loved his mix of witty humor and technical pen game as well as his intense delivery. Dave Denver has also released several singles and collaboration tracks under RNP Productions.

emcees.name: Deadline
emcees.bio: Deadline began making an impact as a battle emcee at Gerahay Letra, an Iloilo-based league. His overall skills were enough to get him a spot at the Won Minutes Visayas event in early 2023. He faced Lawrence at the event, gaining a unanimous decision victory. His big stage debut took place at Gubat 12 in September 2023, where he won against Crypto. Deadline's impressive rhyme schemes, style breakdowns, technical lines, and aggression were enough to garner him a huge following. He has also recorded a few tracks, which you can listen to on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Dello
emcees.bio: Dello made his debut at the first Second Sight and even though he lost, the audience was still captivated by his jokes and multi-syllabic rhymes. He then showed his off-the-dome skills in his battle with Target at the inaugural Ahon event. Dello proved that despite of the modern format of battle rap, you can still win by freestyling. It was the night where he was crowned the official “rebuttal king” of FlipTop. The Tondo emcee also has an impressive music career. So far, he has released a solo mixtape and album as well as a project with his group Skwaterhawz.

emcees.name: Dhuski
emcees.bio: Dhuski officially joined the FlipTop roster after a great performance at the fifth Process of Illumination tryouts in Metro Manila. He debuted at Aspakan 3, scoring a 4-1 win against Sur Henyo. Apart from his sick rebuttals, fans also enjoyed his creative humor. The Bulacan-based emcee improved his pen game further in his next battles. He may have lost against Hazky at Aspakan 4, but the crowd was still entertained by his gimmicks, particularly the “body language” scheme.

emcees.name: Dilim
emcees.bio: After an impressive showing at Process of Illumination 5 in Calabarzon, Dilim from Laguna immediately became part of FlipTop's official roster. He battled Mikidee in his debut and won by unanimous decision. The crowd thoroughly enjoyed his combination of creative jokes and serious punchlines. He and Sibil made an impact at the 2017 Dos Por Dos Tournament by scoring an upset victory over Jonas and Lhipkram in the first round. They may have lost in the quarterfinals, but they still managed to captivate the crowd from start to finish.

emcees.name: Dodong Saypa
emcees.bio: Dodong Saypa was already very active in battle rap before joining FlipTop. Some of the leagues he has competed in include Motus, Insane, Siren, FRBL, and Lyricus. His FlipTop debut took place at Won Minutes Luzon 2024 2, where he faced CRhyme. He then proceeded to the big stage, facing Shaboy at Unibersikulo 12. He lost both matches, but still ended up being a crowd favorite. On Ahon 15 Day 3, he secured his first victory against Tulala. While the comedic style is nothing new in FlipTop, Dodong Saypa makes sure to introduce something unique in every match. His playful delivery adds more effectivity to his jokes.

emcees.name: Don Pao
emcees.bio: Don Pao first made an impact in 2017 after joining Bahay Katay's tournament and eventually winning the championship. He finally made his FlipTop debut in December 2021 at Ahon 12, the year's biggest event. The Shots Fired Kartel representative faced Zaki in a widely-acclaimed match. Don Pao won the battle with his trademark calm delivery and impressive mix of gun bars and solid punches. Apart from battle rap, Don Pao is also a force to be reckoned with on the music side. He has released various tracks and music videos, all of which gained huge numbers on YouTube. The MV for “Pera in this Bitch”, which features him, Kris Delano, Tiny Montana, and Pricetagg, has now exceeded 2 million views.

emcees.name: Dopee
emcees.bio: Dopee is one of the first emcees in Davao to battle in FlipTop. He took on Mac T at the inaugural Different Ways event and went home with a split decision victory. At 082 Magnitude, he battled Wangbo Loco and once again got the win. His confident presence and his unorthodox humor quickly became his biggest strengths. Dopee also participated in two Dos Por Dos tournaments: 2012 with Malupit and 2013 with Snob. Despite losing both competitions, he was still able to entertain the crowd. Even before joining the league, Dopee has been active in making music. He has released various solo tracks as well as songs with his groups Speech and Kalawakan Krew. In July 2015, he dropped his solo EP entitled “Eping”. You can listen to it on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Dosage
emcees.bio: Dosage is one of the most renowned artists in Davao's underground hip-hop scene. His music alone earned him a spot in the league's roster. He made his FlipTop debut in 2015, facing Tatz Maven in an epic encounter. Despite losing the battle, fans appreciated his aggressive presence and superb leftfield lyricism. He continued showcasing his unorthodox style in his next bouts. Apart from being an emcee, Dosage is also a respected producer. His beats are dark and menacing, and he never conformed to the more popular, mainstream sound. He has released various instrumental albums as well as an EP and LP with his group Kalawakan Krew.

emcees.name: Duma
emcees.bio: Despite not winning the championship at the Central Luzon Process of Illumination tryouts in 2018, Duma still earned a spot at the league's roster thanks to his solid performance. He faced SlockOne on his debut battle at Won Minutes and won via unanimous decision. Fans quickly become hooked on his impressive flow and unorthodox angles and punches. After a brief hiatus from battling, Duma made his return on September 2021. He took on Illtimate and even though he lost the match, many applauded his improved pen game. Duma's battle rap journey is just getting started.

emcees.name: EJ Power
emcees.bio: Despite not reaching the finals of the Process of Illumination in Central Luzon, Bataan's EJ Power was still accepted into the roster thanks to his solid performance. In his debut battle against Rich Flo at Aspakan 3, he showed everyone that he truly belongs in FlipTop. Battle rap fans were astounded by his blend of creative humor and technical rhymes. He's also impressive when it comes to switching flows. You'll often see him rap at a moderate pace in the beginning and then, go faster towards the end. His battle with LilJohn at Bwelta Balentong 3 is often considered to be his best performance to date.

emcees.name: Elbiz
emcees.bio: Elbiz made his first appearance at the inaugural Dos Por Dos with Frooz. They lost at the quarterfinals, but at the second tournament, they were able to bounce back by winning the championship. Their most notable victory was against the tandem of Abra and Apekz. Elbiz debuted as a solo emcee at Aspakan 1, scoring an impressive victory against Jaffie. Whether it's 1-on-1 or 2-on-2, the QC-born rapper is sure to astound you with his intelligent humor, smooth flow, and well-constructed multis.

emcees.name: Emar Industriya
emcees.bio: Emar Industriya is one of the few emcees in FlipTop who represents the leftfield style of battling to the fullest. He instantly became part of the roster after an impressive performance at the Process of Illumination 5 in Metro Manila. The wordsmith from Cavite debuted at Kataga 3, where he won against Castyboy by unanimous decision. He then faced Ilaya at Ahon 8 in a battle many consider to be the most thought-provoking in the league. Fans often claim that his battle against Zero Hour at Pakusganay 5 was his best performance yet. What makes him one-of-a-kind is not only his effective Spoken Word-type delivery, but his intricate vocabulary as well. In December of 2016, Emar released his debut solo album entitled “Industriyalismo”. The project was critically-acclaimed, thanks to its powerful lyrics and enthralling production. He's also an active member of Uprising Records. Expect to hear more from him on the music side.

emcees.name: Empithri
emcees.hometown: Surigao City, SDN & Babybay City, Leyte
emcees.bio: Empithri is the first emcee from Surigao to battle in FlipTop's Gubat event. After his impressive performance, there's no doubt we will see more of him in the league. Empithri first gained recognition by becoming the 2019 SURB League Champion. He was one of the special picks of the Process of Illumination 7 in Visayas and made his debut at Gubat 11, taking on Ban in a close battle. He may have lost the bout, but fans admired his technical pen game, brilliant humor, and confident presence. Aside from battle rap, Empithri also aims to make a mark in music. He raps in Bisaya and English and has recorded over 40 tracks. You can listen to his songs and watch his music videos on his official YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Fangs
emcees.bio: Fangs joined the FlipTop roster after impressing everyone at the Ubec Mindfields Tryouts. His first match was against Zeus in the Bisaya Conference, where he emerged victorious in dominating fashion. The Cebuano emcee proceeded to battle in Filipino, and his consecutive wins are proof that his technical rapping style and unique humor works. Despite losing to Mhot at Ahon 7, he is the only emcee so far who came close to beating the crowd favorite. His match with Marshall Bonifacio at Gubat 9 is often regarded as one of the best battles of 2019. Apart from battling, Fangs is also killing it in the music scene. He released his solo album “Salamin” in 2016, which includes the famous track “Delikado”.

emcees.name: Fernie
emcees.bio: Fernie started out in the underground battle rap scene. In 2019, he won the Sunugan Kalye Championship, defeating Blonskie in a back-and-forth bout. The Tondo emcee has also competed in Alyansa, Motus, and Bahay Katay. He made his FlipTop debut at Won Minutes Luzon 2024, scoring a victory against Freek in a solid match. Despite losing in his next two battles against Pamoso and Jamy Sykes respectively, his skills still captivated the viewers. He became known for his impressive multisyllabic rhymes, well-rounded pen game, and creative angles.

emcees.name: Flict-G
emcees.bio: Flict-G is another name that comes to mind when talking about the best speed rappers in the country. Just like Smugglaz, he was already spitting rapid fire flows way before the league started. So when FlipTop finally began, Flict-G was invited to compete at the Down N South event. He was unsuccessful in his debut match, but in 2012, he came back with an improved pen game and flow. Since then, Flict-g continues to make an impact in every battle that he's in. His Gubat 5 match against Damsa is already considered a classic and even though he lost, fans still applauded his epic performance. He was a semi-finalist at the 2013 Isabuhay Tournament and at the 2017 Dos Por Dos (with Damsa). He also released a few songs and music videos, all of which are available online.

emcees.name: Frooz
emcees.bio: Frooz debuted at the inaugural Dos Por Dos Tournament in 2012 with Elbiz. They lost at the quarterfinals, but in 2013, they joined again and became the champions. Frooz also made a huge impact in FlipTop as a solo emcee. In every match that he's in, he always mixes technical lines with creative humor. Battle rap fans got hooked to his style when he went one-on-one with Silencer. When he's not in the battle stage or pit, Frooz makes music with his group Tha Green House. Their mixtape “Greendependence Day” was released in 2017 and can be heard on YouTube.

emcees.name: Fukuda
emcees.bio: CDO's Fukuda officially joined the league's roster after showcasing his rapping skills at the Mindfields Tryouts in Mindanao. His pen game vastly improved at the 2017 and 2018 Isabuhay tournaments, which led him to the semi finals. He may not have won the championship on both occassions, but he was still able to make an impact with his enhanced technical rapping style and aggressive delivery. His quarterfinals match with Batas is where he truly went beast mode. Fukuda also shows dedication in music. He and his SouthDoggz crew released their first album called “Rebirth of the Underground” in early 2014.

emcees.name: G-Clown
emcees.bio: G-Clown made his FlipTop debut at Kataga, beating J-Lem with his swift flow, aggressive delivery, and complex multis. His trademark style clicked with the audience, and he improved it further in his next battles. At the first round of the 2016 Isabuhay Tournament, he went face-to-face with the very popular Loonie. He may have lost, but many consider it to be his best performance in FlipTop. In 2019, he once again joined the tournament and was able to reach the semi-finals. G-Clown is also highly skilled when it comes to jokes. Watch his match against Frooz and expect to laugh out loud from the first to the third round.

emcees.name: Gameboy
emcees.bio: Kidapawan City's Gameboy first emerged in the scene as an active battler in various underground leagues in Mindanao. He joined the Process of Illumination tryouts in 2018 where he became one of the special picks of the night. For his FlipTop debut, he took on Sael and won via unanimous decision. He faced Dopee in his second match and delivered the shocker of the night by defeating the veteran emcee. Since his debut, fans and fellow rappers have been giving Gameboy props for his overall rap ability. He effortlessly combines heavy-hitting lines with comedic bars and he spits these rhymes with the utmost confidence. His solid lyricism can also be heard on his music which you can check out online.

emcees.name: GI
emcees.bio: Before FlipTop, GI was already a well-known battle emcee in the Cebu-based league Rapollo. He joined the 2018 Process of Illumination in Visayas and become one of the special picks. His debut match took place at Gubat 7, facing Munchito in a Bisaya battle. He won via unanimous decision. Since then, GI has been entertaining the crowd with his witty sense of humor, clever angles, and sharp delivery. He also remains active in various underground leagues in his hometown.

emcees.name: GL
emcees.bio: GL made a name for himself in Visayas' hip-hop scene by participating in underground battle leagues. He then competed at the 2018 Process of Illumination event in Cebu and won the championship. His first match took place at Gubat 8 against Pen Pluma. Despite losing the battle, the fans and emcees applauded his incredible performance. Since his debut, GL has been gaining not only more wins but also more supporters. Apart from his extensive vocabulary, he quickly became known for his intelligent, well-constructed angles such as the now influential "train of thought" schemes. In 2024, he joined the Isabuhay Tournament, giving game-changing performances that effortlessly got him to the finals where he faced Vitrum. After a very close match, GL was hailed as the champion. Outside of battle rap, the Leyte representative still lives and breathes hip-hop. 2022 saw the release of his much-awaited solo EP titled "SA/LIRIKO". The whole project is available on his YouTube channel. It consists of five tracks, with A.D. Beats handling the production.

emcees.name: Goriong Talas
emcees.bio: Spade, now known as Goriong Talas, immediately became well-known after winning the inaugural FlipTop tryouts in 2010. In his debut at Down N South, he was able to showcase his raw aggression and complex rhymes. Casual fans usually overlook his pen game, but once you dissect his lines, you will see how creative and lethal he is. The 2021 Isabuhay Tournament saw Talas in his most effective form yet. He took on J-Blaque in the finals and despite not winning the championship, his performance was still widely-acclaimed. Musically, he and his group Illustrado remain as one of the most renowned hardcore acts in the scene. They've released two albums so far, with the latest ("Hanggang Kamatayan: Ngayon at Bukas") being the first-ever double LP to be produced in Philippine hip-hop.

emcees.name: Harlem
emcees.bio: Harlem's first FlipTop appearance was at Second Sight in 2010, where he won against Apekz in a freestyle match. From there, he continued battling and scored a few noteworthy victories. The Pasig-based rapper became well-known not only for his confident delivery, but for his complex multis, witty jokes, and hard punches as well. In 2012, he and Juan Lazy decided to participate at the Dos Por Dos Tournament. The duo lost at the finals, but there's no doubt that they made the contest much more entertaining. Their battles with Apoc and Dhictah and Papew and Melchrist are now considered classics. Harlem made his return to battling in 2020, maintaining his multisyllabic rhyming ability and intense stage presence. His battle with Zend Luke is a candidate for battle of the year (2021). When he's not on the battle stage, Harlem is active in music. He and his group Schizophrenia have released a number of tracks, all of which enjoyed considerable success. The music video for their song “Masarap” now has over 5 million views on YouTube.

emcees.name: Hazky
emcees.bio: Antipolo's Hazky joined the fourth Process of Illumination 4 in 2014, and after an impressive showing, he became part of the main roster. He proved that he wasn't a fluke when he scored a 5-0 victory against Nerdskillz at Kataga 2. Up to now, he continues to impress everyone with his mixture of jokes and serious lines. Hazky also makes sure that he keeps the crowd entertained with his on-stage antics. His popular gimmicks include the Hentai Kamen costume against Mikidee and Martin and the mistress character against Shernan. The latter now has over 37 million views. Hazky participated in the 2023 Isabuhay Tournament, introducing fans to his much improved well-rounded style. Despite losing against Invictus at the finals, no one can deny his impressive performance throughout. He also has a popular YouTube channel called “Hazky TV”. It now contains over 230,000 subscribers.

emcees.name: Hearty
emcees.bio: Hearty instantly made history on her debut. Her match with Lil Sisa is the first ever female emcee battle in FlipTop. She became part of the league after Anygma heard her underground hits online. After the Lil Sisa match, Hearty's pen game continued to improve. Her undeniable charisma adds more impact to her confrontational bars. She also incorporates humor to her verses while maintaining her aggressive aura. Apart from FlipTop, Hearty enjoyed considerable success in leagues such as Bahay Katay and Sunugan. Right now, she's an active content creator. You can check out her vlogs on her YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Hespero
emcees.bio: Hespero of Quezon City started his battle rap career by making an impact in leagues such as PULO, BLVCKOUT, and Motus. His solid performances were enough to get him a spot at the first Won Minutes Luzon 2024 event. He defeated Saint Ice in what is considered by many as one of the best bouts of the night. Hespero made his big stage debut at Zoning 17, scoring a victory against Frinze in a back-and-forth match. His well-rounded pen game combined with his complex rhyming method instantly gained him a large following. You can also check out his music on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Icaruz
emcees.bio: Icaruz's first appearance was at the Bara Ko, Barako event in December of 2011, where he defeated Elias by unanimous decision. FlipTop fans were instantly enthralled by his raw aggression and brutal, in-your-face lines. He then decided to incorporate a little bit of humor into his style, making him a more effective battle emcee. His biggest 1-on-1 match was against Tipsy D at Ahon 4 and even though he lost, many claim that it was a very close fight. In 2013, he and Rapido teamed up at the Dos Por Dos Tournament and were able to reach the semifinals.

emcees.name: Ilaya
emcees.bio: Even before FlipTop began, Ilaya is already a respected wordsmith. He was part of the legendary group Tao Sa Laya and has worked with veterans Los Indios Bravos on several occasions. The Taguig-based emcee officially became part of FlipTop in February of 2014, after impressing the audience with his strong performance at Process of Illumination 4. He proved that he definitely belongs to the battle scene when he defeated Left Eye Blind in his debut. Fans of the league praised not only his complex Filipino vocabulary, but also his raw aggression. His most recent battle was against Sayadd at Ahon 10. Ilaya's dedication to music didn't stop or slow down at all. He and Tala, collectively known as Kartel, are released their debut album “Kontrapunto” under Uprising. The duo is also well-known for their collaboration with Reggae band Lion and the Scouts. They released an album in early 2014 called “Pagsibol”, which features the popular track “Pag-asa, Pag-ibig, Paglaya”.

emcees.name: Illtimate
emcees.bio: Illtimate gained a small following in the underground scene after competing in different amateur battle leagues in the country. The Pampanga-based emcee quickly became well-known for his captivating pen game. In 2018, he joined the Process of Illumination tryouts and despite not winning the tournament, he became part of the special picks. Illtimate finally made his debut at the inaugural Won Minutes event, where he took on Vitrum. Their clash is often considered as the battle of the night by fellow emcees and fast. Illtimate continued battling in the pandemic era, gaining impressive wins against Luxuria and Duma. His delivery may be laidback most of the time, but his rhyme schemes and punches remain deadly.

emcees.name: Invictus
emcees.bio: Invictus is one of the emcees that lifted the “Basta Gapo, bano” curse. He joined the 2015 Process of Illumination in Central Luzon, and even though he didn't become the champion, his hard-hitting performance landed him a spot in the league's roster. Apart from his aggressive delivery, Invictus is also famous for his complex (and often overlooked) wordplays and brutal lines. He's always in top form in every battle; proof of this is when he joined the 2023 Isabuhay Tournament. Invictus faced Hazky in the finals and dominantly won the championship.

emcees.name: J-Blaque
emcees.bio: J-Blaque was one of the standouts at the Process of Illumination 5 tryouts in Cebu. He was part of the special picks, and his first official battle took place at Gubat 5 against Aelekz. The emcee from Lapu-Lapu City lost his debut battle, but it further motivated him to be a better lyricist. Since then, J-Blaque has been collecting wins with his perfect mix of wordplays, humor, and straight-up aggression. The 2020 Isabuhay Tournament is where J-Blaque officially became a top emcee. Many doubted him when the lineup was released, but once the competition began, he proved everyone wrong. He faced Goriong Talas at the finals and ended up winning the championship in a back-and-forth match.

emcees.name: J-King
emcees.bio: On the 7 th of August 2015, J-King travelled from Cabanatuan to Metro Manila just to participate at the 5 th Process of Illumination. Now that's what you call dedication. He showed his supreme freestyling skills and ended up winning the whole thing. J-King proved that he wasn't a fluke when he finally debuted at Aspakan 3. His comedic delivery and brilliant mixture of jokes and technical lines quickly made him a fan favorite. He and Romano joined the 2017 Dos Por Dos Tournament and were able to give a memorable performance. Despite losing against Sinio and Tipsy D at the semi finals, the duo still earned the respect of the viewers, some of which claim that they should've won.

emcees.name: J-Skeelz
emcees.bio: Before FlipTop emerged, J-Skeelz was already making waves in the rap game with his group 187 Mobstaz. The veteran emcee joined the league in late 2011 and quickly became a crowd favorite thanks to his heavy bars and intimidating voice. His match against Batas in August 2012 remains to be popular among fans of battle rap. Instead of busting hurtful lines in the aforementioned contest, J-Skeelz taught his opponent the meaning for respect. Not only was his approach effective, but it was also very unique during that time. The Tondo-born rapper is also untouchable when it comes to freestyle. At Ahon 8, he managed to defeat Khen Magat by spitting off-the-dome lines from the first to the third round.

emcees.name: Jamy Sykes
emcees.bio: Jamy Sykes first made his presence known in underground leagues such as Motus and Word War. His Process of Illumination 7 entry earned him a spot in FlipTop's roster. The Olongapo representative took on Cygus on his debut in the league, and even though he lost, the battle was critically-acclaimed. He then faced Fernie at Zoning 18, and scored a unanimous decision victory. Apart from his rapid-fire flow, Jamy Sykes became known for his sharp vocabulary and innovative metaphors. He's also active in music. His solo EP “Crumble” was released on streaming sties on the 21st of December 2021.

emcees.name: Jawz
emcees.bio: Jawz of Tondo gained recognition in the underground battle scene after joining Motus and FRBL, where he won the championship at the fourth 1UP Tournament. He made his first FlipTop appearance at Won Minutes Luzon 2 against Pamoso in a showcase of pure lyricism. Jawz then made his big stage debut at Unibersikulo 12, winning against Bisente in a back-and-forth verbal brawl. His innovative wordplay and metaphors as well as his strong stage presence are his biggest strengths. Jawz is also passionate when it comes to making music. He has released numerous tracks, two of which are collaborations with Juan and Kyle. These are the hit songs “Marikit sa Dilim” and Sa'yo Lang”.

emcees.name: JDee
emcees.bio: JDee started out as a battle emcee in Bataan's underground scene. In 2018, he joined FlipTop's Central Luzon tryouts and was able to reach the finals. Despite not winning the championship, his performance was still enough for him to earn a spot in the league's roster. JDee's first official battle took place at the 2019 Won Minutes event, taking on his tryout finals opponent CNine. He lost his debut match, but it only made him even stronger. The pandemic failed to halt JDee's plan on elevating his battle rap career. He became active at the quarantine battles and quickly made an impact with his dominant victories. The Bataan-born emcee became well-known for his blend of comedic and technical lines and clever rebuttals as well as his powerful delivery. You can always expect an intense atmosphere whenever he's battling.

emcees.name: Jonas
emcees.bio: Here's a trivia, Jonas' FlipTop debut was actually in 2011 at the Bara Ko, Barako event. He lost his first battle and suddenly fell off the radar. In 2015, Jonas re-emerged at Process of Illumination 5, where he reached the finals. The league once again welcomed him to the roster, and from there, he was able to redeem himself from his 2011 loss. His humorous bars are delivered with a comedic tone, which makes him stand out from the other jokers in FlipTop. Despite losing against Lhipkram at the semi-finals of the 2020 Isabuhay Tournament, Jonas' witty lines continue to be quoted by fans on social media.

emcees.name: JP
emcees.bio: JP is relatively new to battle rap, having only competed once in a Gensan-based underground league. Nevertheless, his Process of Illumination 7 entry and his music are enough to get him a spot in FlipTop. JP made his debut at Pakusganay 7, taking on Sickreto. He may have lost his first battle in the league, but fans got a glimpse of his creative pen game and angles as well as his unpredictable flow. As stated above, JP is active when it comes to both rapping and producing. His group Tugmang Krimen continues to make waves in the Gensan hip-hop scene. He has also released several solo songs, all of which are available on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: JR Zero
emcees.bio: JR Zero was one of the special picks at the 2018 Process of Illumination tryouts in Davao. He then competed at two Won Minutes events in Mindanao, winning both by unanimous decision. His rapid-fire flow and well-constructed multis continue to be his biggest strengths. The pandemic didn't stop JR Zero from accepting more matches. He was active during the quarantine battles era and despite a few loses, his overall rap ability still manages to enthrall viewers. Apart from battle rap, JR Zero is also very active in music. He's part of the rap trio 3 DIgitz together with Jai and the 2019 Isabuhay Champion Sixth Threat. They've released a few singles online, the most famous of which is “Pilipinong Wack”. 3 Digitz was signed to the legendary label Dongalo Wreckords on September 2020. As for his solo career, JR Zero has some solid bangers available on Spotify.

emcees.name: K-Ram
emcees.bio: K-Ram was a special pick at the 2018 Calabarzon Process of Illumination tryouts. He battled One Lie Ace on his debut battle and got a unanimous decision win. Since then, K-Ram continued his FlipTop journey, scoring more impressive victories along the way. He is now well-known for his complex multis, clear delivery, and always-effective humor. K-Ram is also active when it comes to music. He appeared on various tracks from fellow battle emcees and releases a few solo bangers. The music video for his song “Arkila” now has over 40,000 views on YouTube.

emcees.name: Kalixs
emcees.bio: Bulacan's Kalixs started his battle career by competing in underground leagues such as Rap Conquer and Motus. His remarkable performances earned him a spot in the Won Minutes Luzon 2024 2 lineup. He won against Razick in a very close and entertaining match. His next battle took place at Second Sight 13, where he faced Dave Denver. The emcee from Unknown wasn't victorious, but the crowd still lauded his performance. His impressive wordplay and metaphors combined with his strong presence make him a credible threat in the league.

emcees.name: Kamandag
emcees.bio: Kamangdag made his FlipTop debut at the very first event in Olongapo (Gapo De Gulat). He lost against KJah in a one-sided affair, but that didn't stop him from continuing his battle rap journey. Kamandag's next battle took place at Ahon 2, where he scored a 4-1 victory against Raynoa. His pen game is more teknikal and his delivery is one of the most aggressive at that time. He secured more impressive wins in the next two years. He's currently inactive now, but hopefully, he'll make a comeback very soon! Despite his battle rap hiatus, Kamandag remains active in making music. He and his group SKRMSHTRXXPZ released their debut album “Sa Kuko ng Nakaambang Gitnang Daliri” on July 2019. Two months later, he dropped his solo LP “Makamandag ng Sining”. You can check them out on all streaming sites.

emcees.name: Karisma
emcees.bio: Karisma immediately became one of the most promising emcees in the Philippine underground battle rap scene after an impressive stint at Pulo's Titulo Tournament in 2022. He was able to reach the finals and despite not winning the championship, he still left the viewers in awe with his strong stage presence, clever metaphors, and a perfect mix of comedic and serious concepts. He finally made his FlipTop debut at Second Sight 11, taking on Ruffian. Fans consider it the battle of the night. Karisma is also active in music as part of MM13. You can listen to his solo tracks and collaborations on his crew's YouTube channel. His latest project is the music video for his single HATAW with RawV and KG.

emcees.name: Katana
emcees.bio: Katana first made a name for himself in various underground leagues; his most well-known was his stint at Motus. He made his FlipTop debut in February 2024, competing at the Won Minutes Luzon event. His battle with Crispy Fetus is considered by fans as one of the most entertaining of the year so far. The Las Pinas representative moved up to the big stage at Zoning 17, defeating Meraj in a back-and-forth battle. He then faced Manda Baliw at Bwelta Balentong 11 and scored a 4-1 victory. Katana's popularity grew rapidly, thanks to his unique brand of humor and overall creativity in his pen game. When he's not battling, he's busy writing and recording music. He ended 2024 with a bang by beating the veteran Harlem at Ahon 15. In 2025, he joined the Isabuhay Tournament, where he reached the finals. After an intense, back-and-forth match with Lhipkram, he was declared the champion. Katana won the title on just his second year in the league and with an undefeated record. Now that's an impressive achievement!

emcees.name: Kenzer
emcees.bio: Before joining FlipTop, Kenzer was already battling in various underground leagues such as 053, Asdangay, and Stealth. He made his FlipTop debut at Won Minutes Visayas in 2023, beating Chibi in an entertaining match. The Tacloban City emcee then moved up to the big stage at Gubat 12, scoring another impressive win against Zero MB. He quickly gained a huge following with his combination of creative humor and hard-hitting bars, both of which are delivered flawlessly. Kenzer has also released a few tracks which you can listen to on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Khen Magat
emcees.bio: Khen Magat has been mastering the art of freestyling way before the league started. His undeniable skill immediately caught the attention of the FlipTop staff and in March 2017, he finally made his debut. He took on fellow veteran Abaddon and even though he lost, the audience was still captivated by his confident delivery and combination of sick writtens and freestyles. Some may criticize his current win-loss record, but once he's fully adjusted to the modern format, expect him to come back with a vengeance. Music is also something that Khen Magat is passionate about. He released his solo mixtape called “Filipino Freestyler” in 2008 and has appeared in various projects under Dongalo Wreckords, a label founded by the legendary Andrew E. He's currently the councilor of Pasay City District II, hence his hiatus from hip-hop.

emcees.name: KJap
emcees.bio: KJap is another special pick at the 2015 Process of Illumination tryouts in Central Luzon. He took on Invictus at Aspakan 3 for his first official FlipTop match. Despite losing the battle, KJap still caught the attention of viewers with his impressive arsenal of metaphors and wordplay. He joined the 2016 Isabuhay Tournament but lost in the first round against Plazma. KJap was able to bounce back from his losses by beating Righteous1 and Wrathsol. In July 2022, he finally released his debut solo album entitled “After Timeout”.

emcees.name: Kregga
emcees.bio: Kregga first made his presence felt in 2013 at the FlipTop Mindanao tryouts. The Cagayan de Oro native immediately stood out thanks to his wide vocabulary. He spits these complex lines with a relatively calm delivery, which adds to his uniqueness. Kregga proved that he's a lyrical threat when he faced Cerberus at Ahon 6 and got the W. Since then, he remains one of the most renowned technical emcees in the league. When he's not in the battle rap arena, Kregga makes music as part of Uprising Records and Sumagupa Krew. His debut solo EP entitled "Karo'Mata Epe" was released in November 2018. He maintains his leftfield rapping style in his songs.

emcees.name: Kris Delano
emcees.bio: Formerly known as Hallucinate, Kris Delano officially joined FlipTop in September of 2010, beating Fuego in an English Conference battle. He then decided to showcase his skills in Tagalog by participating at the 2013 Dos Por Dos with Ice Rocks. The duo may have lost the first round, but the crowd still praised their performance. Kris Delano continued to shine at the 2014 Isabuhay Tournament. He was able to reach the semi-finals, thanks to his technical lines and confident stage presence. In 2017, he joined the Dos Por Dos Tournament again, this time with fellow Shots Fired artist PriceTagg. They faced Sinio and Tipsy D in the quarterfinals and even though they didn't get the W, many consider it to be a close fight. Kris Delano's success continued in music. His single “Alak Usok Pera” now has over 4 million views on YouTube and over 5 million plays on Spotify. On June 2021, he released the music video for his song “Pera in this Bitch” featuring Don Pao, Tiny Montana, and Pricetagg. The MV has now exceeded 2 million views.

emcees.name: Lanzeta
emcees.bio: Just like Invictus, Lanzeta also helped Olongapo rise up from all the hate. He first appeared at the Central Luzon Process of Illumination in 2015, where he became champion. Since then, he has been leaving audiences in awe with his rapid fire flow and intricately-constructed bars. The raw aggression in his delivery also makes him stand out from FlipTop's roster. In his battle with Pistolero at Ahon 8, he proved to everyone that he can spit jokes without abandoning his hardcore style. There's no denying that Lanzeta is one of the most unpredictable in the league.

emcees.name: Lax Hartis
emcees.hometown: Sta. Ana, Manila & San Andres, Bukid
emcees.bio: Lax Hartis became well-known in the underground battle rap scene after winning the championship at Pulo Rap Battle League's Titulo Tournament in 2022. His performance earned him membership on FipTop's official roster. He has the ability to brilliantly mix humorous and heavy bars and his multisyllabic rhyming style is simply awe-inspiring. Lax Hartis finally made his debut at Second Sight 11, the league's first event of 2023. He took on fellow promising emcee Class G.

emcees.name: Lemi
emcees.bio: Lemi first made his presence known in Bahay Katay and Sunugan, where he won the championship by beating the veteran M Zhayt. In 2018, he participated in the Process of Illumination 6 Metro Manila tryouts and became one of the special picks. His debut battle took place at Won Minutes in March 2019, taking on C-Quence in a highly-entertaining match. Fans quickly admired his clear delivery and his flawless mix of technical and comedic rhymes.

emcees.name: Lhipkram
emcees.bio: Lhipkram got accepted into the league after a remarkable performance at the Process of Illumination 5 in Metro Manila. He lost his debut battle against Doc Pau, but was able to bounce back at Second Sight 4 by defeating El Quiel. Apart from his freestyle skills, he also became well-known for his creative jokes, complex multis, and impeccable flow. He unleashed his full form when he joined the 2020 Isabuhay Tournament. His pen game was better than ever, eventually leading to a historic finals match with fellow 3GS member M Zhayt. He continued his dominant streak and in 2025, he gave the tournament another shot. Once again, he reached the finals, taking on Katana in a back-and-forth match. Outside of the battle scene, Lhipkram is busy making music. His single “Don Joaquin” dropped in May of 2020, and currently has over 240,000 views on YouTube. He's also one of the founding members of TEAM PINSAN TV. Their channel, which has 256,000 subscribers, features music videos, singles, reactions, and various comedic content.

emcees.name: Lil Sisa
emcees.bio: Don't be deceived by her girl-next-door look. On the battle stage, Lil Sisa can dismantle you with her confident delivery and brilliant mixture of bars and jokes. She debuted at the Sabong Sumulong event, scoring a unanimous decision victory against fellow femcee Hearty. At Ahon 7, Lil Sisa proved that she's as good as the boys by defeating Shernan. She only has two battles in the league so far, but remains to be one of the most popular emcees in FlipTop. As for her music, you can check them all out online including her music video for “Melodiya”.

emcees.name: LilJohn
emcees.bio: LilJohn was already killing it in freestyle battles way before FlipTop began. So when he joined Process of Illumination 4 in 2014, he was able to reach the finals and became co-champion (with M Zhayt) easily. He even joined the Process of Illumination 5 in Cebu just for fun and won the championship as well. Ever since his debut battle, LilJohn has been entertaining fans with his humorous approach to battling. If he's facing a “serious” opponent, expect him to bust a few satirical bars. You can see him using this style in his match with Lanzeta at Aspakan 4. Unfortunately, in October 2019, he tragically passed away. Rest in peace, LilJohn. Thanks for the memories!

emcees.name: LilStrocks
emcees.bio: LilStrocks first gained recognition by competing at Rapollo, a battle league based in Cebu. In 2018, he decided to participate at the Visayas Process of Illumination tryouts and ended up as a special pick. He faced Jorer on his debut battle and the loud crowd reactions are enough to say that he gave a great performance. Up to now, the Bohol native remains active in the league. LilStrocks instantly became one of the Visayas Division's most renowned emcees thanks to his clever angles and witty comedic style. He's one of the few rappers who can spit funny bars consecutively without sounding too forced. LilStrocks has also released a few songs which you can check out on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: LilWeng
emcees.bio: LilWeng started making waves in Laglagan, an underground league established in 2016. He joined the 2018 Process of Illumination tryouts in Calabarzon where he became the champion. Since then, the Laguna-based emcee has been showcasing his witty comedic style and heavy bars. Each punchline is more effective thanks to his confident and aggressive delivery. He's also busy on the music side of things. His solo tracks as well as his collaborations are available on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Loonie
emcees.bio: Loonie made his FlipTop debut at the first Second Sight event, and he already proved that he's a top-tier emcee. A few rappers attempted to copy his signature multisyllabic rhymes, but he remains to be the best to do it. His impressive skill set and charisma are what made him the most viewed in the whole world. Loonie also has the capability to come up with clever angles, which can be seen in his battle against Tipsy D at Bwelta Balentong 3. He then cemented his legacy as one of the greatest when he became the Isabuhay Champion in 2016. Outside of the battle scene, Loonie continues to be active in music. He released two solo albums and two projects with his band Stick Figgas so far.

emcees.name: Lord Manuel
emcees.bio: Formerly known as Benggamanok, Lord Manuel started making an impact in the underground scene, battling in leagues such as Tietest, Raplines, and FRBL. He instantly became a controversial figure due to his hard-hitting, in-your-face style. In 2022, he participated in FRBL's 1UP Tournament and won the championship. His FlipTop debut took place on the 24th of February 2024 at Won Minutes Luzon. He defeated Meraj in what many consider the best battle in the event. Lord Manuel's next match in the league was against Philos at Unibersikulo 12. He wasn't able to get the W but it was a close bout. The TRNGL member remained ruthless in his bars while showcasing more effective aggression in his delivery. Apart from battle rap, Lord Manuel actively makes music as an emcee and producer. He has released a few EPs, albums, and mixtapes, which you can check out on his YouTube channel. Lyrics-wise, his tracks also have that confrontational vibe as his battles.

emcees.name: Luxuria
emcees.bio: Luxuria started her battle rap career in Sunugan. She quickly stood out thanks to her intimidating presence and impeccable rap skills. The Rizal-born emcee decided to join the 2018 Process of Illumination tryout and became one of the special picks. Her first official battle took place at the inaugural Won Minutes event, where she defeated Bagsik. She remained active since then, beating big names such as Frooz and Batas during the quarantine battles era. Her intensity and her multisyllabic rhymes continue to leave the viewers in awe. She made history at Ahon 13 by becoming the very first femcee to reach the finals of the Isabuhay Tournament. Despite not winning the championship, fans applaud her dominant performance all throughout the competition. When she's not battling, Luxuria is busy with her two businesses. She has her own clothing line (Unlock) and a bagnet bagoong brand, both of which are successful nationwide. She's also currently working on new music. Watch out for that!

emcees.name: M Zhayt
emcees.bio: M Zhayt proved that he's a solid freestyler when he became champion at FlipTop Process of Illumination 4. When he made his debut at Second Sight 2, he showed everyone that his writtens are as good as his off-the-dome rhymes. M Zhayt often switches from freestyle to writtens and vice versa, making him a truly unpredictable emcee. He's also effective in 2-on-2 battles, which is obvious at the 2017 Dos Por Dos Tournament. With their undeniable chemistry, he and Shernan beat Tipsy D and Sinio to become the undisputed champions. The 2020 Isabuhay Tournament cemented M Zhayt's legacy as one of the very best in the league. He brought his A-game up to the epic final round match with Lhipkram and ended up with the crown. As of now, M Zhayt is the only emcee who won all three Process of Illumination, Dos Por Dos, and Isabuhay Championships.

emcees.name: Makii
emcees.bio: Makii is a finalist at the Ubec Mindfields Tryouts, and despite not winning the championship, his amazing performance still earned him a spot in FiipTop's roster. He has several impressive wins under his belt, the most recent of which was against GI in a Tagalog and Bisaya match. Apart from his remarkable rhyme schemes and witty bars, he is also well-known for his clear and hard-hitting delivery. When he's not battling, Makii is focused on making music. You can listen to his solo tracks on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Malupit
emcees.bio: Malupit made his FlipTop debut in 2011 at the inaugural Different Ways event. Despite losing against Don Busabos, he still managed to give an enjoyable performance. The Davao rapper continued battling since then, competing in singles and 2-on-2 matches. His energetic stage presence combined with his heavy bars and witty jokes is his biggest strength. After a brief hiatus, he returned to FlipTop in 2019, beating Mardszen in a very entertaining bout. On June 2016, Malupit finally released his debut solo album “Flow”. He continues to make music now, doing solos and collaborating with his group Karabineros and other artists from his hometown. He has his own recording studio called K Records. Expect to hear more projects from him soon!

emcees.name: Manda Baliw
emcees.bio: Manda Baliw joined the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts in Metro Manila. He wasn't able to advance to the next round, but that didn't stop him from pursuing his hip-hop dreams. The Antipolo emcee continued battling in leagues such as Motus, FRBL, and Sunugan. He amassed a huge following with his witty comedic style that is reminiscent of FlipTop in 2010. His deadpan delivery makes his humor even more effective. He eventually caught the attention of Anygma in mid 2022, which led to his first match in the league against Bagsik. Manda Baliw won his debut battle and instantly became popular among FlipTop fans. He has released plenty of solo and group tracks online, showing his versatility as a lyricist. His latest is a collaboration with Toistorii and Lein entitled “Lasing Ka Na Naman”. Check out the official music video on YouTube! Apart from rapping, Manda Baliw is also an active tattoo artist.

emcees.name: Marichu
emcees.bio: Marichu first became known for her memorable performances in Motus, Sunugan, and Insane. She made her FlipTop debut at Won Minutes 2024 Luzon 2 in Quezon City, facing Shaboy in an entertaining matchup. The Isabela femcee then joined forces with Aubrey for the Dos Por Dos2 Tournament. Their team reached the semifinals. Her next singles match took place at Zoning 18, where she faced Blizzard in a back-and-forth bout. Despite not getting the W, many admired her solid metaphors, witty humor, and strong stage presence.

emcees.name: Marshall Bonifacio
emcees.bio: Marshall's battle against Sak Maestro in a different league immediately caught the attention of the FlipTop staff. The league gave him an opportunity to prove himself at Process of Illumination 5, and he didn't disappoint. Born in Iligan and currently living in Cebu, Marshall Bonifacio attacks his opponents with impressive technical lines and a hard-hitting delivery. He's highly skilled in character assassination, which can be seen in his duel against Chaliz. His showdown with Fangs at Gubat 9 is considered by many as one of the best battles of 2019. The match was so good the judges decided to vote on a draw.

emcees.name: MastaFeat
emcees.bio: MastaFeat was one of the most well-known names in Bahay Katay. He then decided to join the 2018 Process of Illumination tryouts in Calabarzon. Despite losing at the finals, MastaFeat's performance was still enough to earn him a spot on FlipTop's roster. His debut battle against Numerhus is regarded as one of the best battles of that event. 2020 onwards, MastaFeat has been making an impact in the league. His ability to combine freestyle and written rhymes remains uncanny, and his flow continues to stand out. Fans also admire his brand of humor, which is often unpredictable and highly creative. Expect an entertaining battle whenever he's on the stage or pit.

emcees.name: Maxford
emcees.bio: Maxford already made history in his 2011 debut by being part of the first ever Bisaya Conference battle. He took on Whitey Uno and was able to captivate the audience from rounds 1 to 3. When the Davao-born rapper decided to switch to Tagalog, he became a much bigger threat. He scored back-to-back victories with his deadpan humor, technical lines, and improved delivery. His doubters quickly turned into followers when he defeated heavyweight emcees Sinio and Kregga. When he's not in battle mode, Maxford is busy elevating the hip-hop music scene in his city. He has done various tracks featuring some of Davao's most well-known emcees. You can check out his singles on YouTube.

emcees.name: Melchrist
emcees.bio: Born in Batangas, Melchrist is one of the very few emcees in FlipTop who has the perfect aggressive delivery. Making him even more effective as a battle rapper are his brutal, no-nonsense rhymes. After impressing everyone in 1-on-1 matches, he decided to participate at the 2012 Dos Por Dos with Papew. The duo may have lost in the semifinals, but they still managed to enthrall the crowd all throughout. Melchrist went back to singles action in 2014 by joining the Isabuhay Tournament. He went all out, particularly against Kris Delano, and was able to reach the finals. When he's not demolishing opponents in the battle stage, Melchrist is busy making music.
