He was part of the Bake Mixtape (2010) and has worked on various projects with his crewmates from Mongol Unit. Expect to hear more tracks from him.

emcees.name: Meraj
emcees.bio: Even before joining FlipTop, Meraj was already a dominant force in underground battle rap. He has competed in several respected leagues and gained a sizeable following, thanks to his creative pen game and razor-sharp delivery. In mid 2018, he flew to Dubai to focus on a different career, thus putting his battle rap journey on hold. Meraj shocked the scene when he came back to the Philippines and finally made his FlipTop debut at the first Won Minutes Luzon 2024 event. Despite losing to Lord Manuel, many viewers appreciated his impressive performance. He then headed to the big stage at Zoning 17, taking on Katana in an entertaining battle. Meraj momentarily took a break from FlipTop to focus on Motus' Pedestal 3 Tournament. He won the championship on October 26 at Hantungan 4.

emcees.name: Mhot
emcees.bio: Ever since 2015, Mhot has been captivating viewers with his clever use of wordplays (particularly his “anagram” style) and references. He is also highly skilled in freestyling, which he proved at the FlipTop tryouts in Calabarzon. In 2017, Mhot joined the Isabuhay tournament and eventually became the champion. His battle against Sur Henyo is undoubtedly a classic, but the one with Apekz is where he was in top form.

emcees.name: Mikidee
emcees.bio: On the 23rd of October 2015, Mikidee took a trip from Legazpi City to Calabarzon just to join the fifth Process of Illumination. He showed his remarkable freestyle skills, which was enough to make him part of FlipTop's roster. His first official battle was at Kataga 3 in 2016 against Dilim. He failed to get the W, but he was able to entertain the crowd with his creative mix of comedic and serious lines. In 2017, he and fellow Bicolano Wise Wunn participated at the Dos Por Dos Tournament. Despite losing in the first round against M Zhayt and Shernan, the duo still gained the respect of the audience with their chemistry and well-constructed lines. Apart from battle rap, Mikidee also shows dedication in music. His solo album “Masid” was released in early 2018 under Gstyle Wreckords. It consists of 10 tracks, one of which is the thought-provoking “Masid”.

emcees.name: Mimack
emcees.bio: Tacloban's Mimack is already an active battle emcee before becoming part of FlipTop's roster. He has competed in various underground leagues such as 053 and Asdangay. His first battle in FlipTop occurred at Won Minutes Visayas in 2023, where he won against Keji. He then proceeded to the big stage, taking on RG at Gubat 12. In April 2024 at Gubat 13, he faced Deadline in a back-and-forth match. Despite losing both battles, fans were still captivated by his complex schemes, well-rounded writing style, and intense presence. Mimack has also released a few solo and collaboration tracks. Check them out on his YouTube page.

emcees.name: Mistah Lefty
emcees.bio: Before entering the world of battle rap, Mistah Lefty is already a household name in the Visayas hip-hop scene. He has released plenty of hit songs and headlined many sold-out shows in various parts of the country. In November 2022, he made his battle rap debut at RAPOLLO in Cebu, scoring an impressive 5-0 win against Yoex. He then faced Marshall Bonifacio in a back-and-forth promo match. Mistah Lefty finally made his FlipTop debut on the 20th of April 2024 at Gubat 13. The Mandaue City representative took on Kregga, and despite losing the match, the fans still admired his well-rounded pen game, clever schemes, and flawless delivery.

emcees.name: Murdz
emcees.bio: Murdz made a name for himself in the battle rap scene by competing in underground leagues such as Tietest, LURE, and Motus. His first appearance in FlipTop took place on April 2023 at the Won Minutes Visayas event, going against $tep G. After a remarkable performance, he officially became part of the league's roster. Murdz is well-known for his raw aggression and flawless mix of technical and leftfield styles. He has also recently begun writing solo tracks. You can check out his music on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Nadnad
emcees.bio: Representing Cebu and Leyte, Nadnad started his battle rap journey by competing in respected underground leagues such as RAPOLLO and Motus. His FlipTop debut occurred at the Won Minutes Visayas event in early 2023, defeating Nathan in a back-and-forth match. Nadnad's entertaining performance was enough to get him a spot on the big stage. He faced Pen Pluma at Gubat 12, and despite losing, many fans still admired his style. Apart from his strong delivery, he also became known for his effective mixture of heavy bars and witty jokes.

emcees.name: Nathan
emcees.bio: Nathan is already battle-rapping even before joining FlipTop. He started out in Sipalay Rap Republic and Motus, two renowned underground leagues. His first FlipTop appearance was at Won Minutes Visayas in 2023, and even though he was unsuccessful against Nadnad, his impressive performance still got him a spot in the league's roster. Nathan was able to secure his first win at Gubat 13 against Murdz in an entertaining bout. His style is a flawless mix of hard-hitting technical bars and witty comedy. Each line becomes much more impactful, thanks to his confident delivery.

emcees.name: Negatibo
emcees.bio: At the Sabong Sumulong event in November of 2010, veteran emcee Negatibo officially made his FlipTop debut. He took on Daddie Joe D and thanks to his confidence and hard-hitting punchlines, he was able to get the W. Since then, the QC-based rapper remained active in the league and further improved his battling skills. He started to add impressive technical lines and flows to his style, which can be seen in his match with Caliber. Negatibo made an impact not only in the battle scene but in music as well. So far, he has released three solo projects, namely “Anger Management”, “Enlightenment” and the latest one "Entrapment". He also dropped two collaboration albums with F-Dub entitled “The Best of Both Worlds Part 1 and 2”.

emcees.name: Negho Gy
emcees.bio: Negho Gy was already a threat in the underground battle scene. In 2023, he was a finalist at Motus' second Pedestal Tournament. His battle with 3rdy remains one of the most-viewed in the league. He made his FlipTop debut at the first Won Minutes Luzon 2024 event, beating Frinze in an entertaining match. Negho Gy gained another victory at Zoning 17 against Antonym. Fans were quickly astounded by his innovative wordplays and intricate rhyming style. He's also active in making music, having released a few songs and music videos on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Nikki
emcees.bio: Nikki became part of FlipTop's roster after giving a remarkable performance at the 2013 Mindfields Tryouts in Mindanao. Fans of the league instantly got hooked to his rhyme schemes and classic Pinoy humor. This unique style of his is fully displayed in his battle against Silent Effect at the second Pakusganay event. His “gwapo bars” trended in social media for a long period of time, proving Nikki's impact on the viewers. If he's not battling, he makes music with his crew Heneral Luna. Some of their songs are available online.

emcees.name: Numerhus
emcees.bio: Numerhus was already an established name even before FlipTop was founded. He is famous not only for his very impressive flow, but also for his creative song concepts. In 2018, he decided to delve into the world of battle rap by joining the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts. He didn't win the championship, but his rap abilities and confident stage presence were enough for him to be part of the special picks. The Shockra member took on Mastafeat at the first Won Minutes event in 2019, and scored a unanimous decision win. From there, he continued to make waves in the league with his supreme rapping skills. Numerhus may be an active battler now, but he never abandoned his music. He remained consistent when it comes to releasing various projects. He, along with his crew Shockra, released the music video for the track “Operation 10-90”, which now has over 2 million views. On June 2018, Numerhus dropped his debut solo album “Inspired by the Pain”. The LP gained a well-deserved positive reception.

emcees.name: OG Ulo
emcees.bio: OG Ulo is known as a legend in the Quezon City underground battle scene. In 2018, he participated at the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts event and was able to reach second place. The Caloocan-based rapper made his official debut at Won Minutes in 2019, scoring an impressive victory against Crispy Fetus. The crowd admired his unconventional humor and angles as well as his playful delivery. He's on a hiatus from battling as of now, but hopefully, he'll make a comeback very soon!

emcees.name: Onaks
emcees.bio: Onaks immediately made an impact in FlipTop by becoming the champion at the Process of Illumination 5 tryouts event in Calabarzon. He lost his first few battles but was able to bounce back at Bwelta Balentong 7 with a dominating victory against Lil Weng. Onaks introduced a more heavy-hitting approach to his lines, combining it with his aggressive delivery and complex rhyme schemes. At Second Sight 10, he scored another impressive win versus One Lie Ace. Aside from battle rap, Onaks also showcases his top-notch lyricism in his music. His group Yo Gang continues to get props in the underground scene. You can listen to their tracks as well as Onaks' solo bangers on YouTube.

emcees.name: One Lie Ace
emcees.bio: After making a name for himself in the underground battle scene, One Lie Ace decided to join the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts. The emcee from General Trias ended up as one of the special picks of the night. He lost against K-Ram in his debut battle, but it didn't stop him from continuing his battling career. One Lie Ace took a brief hiatus from FlipTop after his first match. He came back a year later with a much improved pen game and a more aggressive delivery. The quarantine battles era saw him scoring impressive wins against Bagsik, SlockOne, and Lemi.

emcees.name: Onlison
emcees.bio: Previously known as Ran, Onlison became part of the FlipTop roster after an impressive showing at the 2013 Mindfields Mindanao Tryouts. His heavy metaphors and witty angles quickly caught the attention of viewers. In his battle with Hizuka, he decided to incorporate comedic elements and was successful at it. His continuous mix of clever jokes and hard-hitting bars made him one of the most versatile emcees in the league today. Battle rap is not the only thing Onlison excels at. He's also a legit threat when it comes to making music. The Tagum and Davao representative has released various solo tracks and has appeared on the Writers' Block Mindanao: Mind The Now compilation album. You can check out his bangers on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Pamoso
emcees.bio: Pamoso is already an active battle emcee before being part of FlipTop, giving standout performances in leagues such as Norte Suprema, PiSO, Sunugan, Motus, and PULO. On May 2024, he finally made his FlipTop debut, taking on FRBL Champion Jawz. Pamoso lost the match but fans were still impressed by his overall style. His next battle took place at Won Minutes Luzon 3, where he scored his first win in the league against Fernie. He joined PULO's Titulo 2024 Tournament and on the 18th of October, he won the championship. His intricate rhyme schemes, combined with impressive wordplays, make him a legit threat. Pamoso is also active in music. You can check out his projects on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Pen Pluma
emcees.bio: Pen Pluma first made an impact as a battle emcee in Rapollo, a league based in his hometown of Cebu. He then joined the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts event in 2018 where he ended up as a special pick. He faced GL in his debut battle and won via split decision. Pen Pluma remained active since then. His latest battle was against Viturm at Ahon 12. Despite losing the aforementioned match, many viewers still applauded his overall performance. Pen Pluma is armed with intricate multis, insane metaphors, and an intense delivery. He's busy making music when he's not on the battle stage. The Cebuano lyricist has released numerous solo and collaboration songs, all of which you can check out online.

emcees.name: Philos
emcees.bio: Like most emcees in FlipTop, Philos first made a name for himself in underground leagues. He has competed in Siksik Bara, RAP KALYE, and Motus. He made his FlipTop debut on May 4, 2024, at Won Minutes Luzon. The Bulacan emcee faced Supremo in a back-and-forth clash. At Unibersikulo 12, he gained his first victory in the league after an intense match with Lord Manuel. There's no denying the impact of his technical rhymes and powerful stage presence. Despite reaching the big stage, Philos never abandoned his underground roots. In the same year as his debut in FlipTop, he competed at Motus' PEDESTAL 3 Tournament, where he reached the finals.

emcees.name: Pistolero
emcees.bio: He may not have won the championship at Process of Illumination 4, but he was still accepted into the main roster thanks to his amazing performance. Tondo's Pistolero won the hearts of FlipTop fans with his heavy bars and superhuman freestyle skills. No matter how hard your line is, he will strike back with consecutive rebuttals. His clashes with Shehyee at Second Sight 3 and at the 2018 Isabuhay Tournament semi-finals are considered classics. At Ahon 13, he officially became a top-tier emcee by finally winning the Isabuhay Championship. Pistolero released his critically-acclaimed debut solo album “25 Anyos” on Feb 28, 2021. The music video for the track “Day Off” gained over 300,000 views, just one month after it was uploaded on YouTube. Pistolero is also the owner and CEO of Bling PH, an online store selling top-quality jewelry and watches.

emcees.name: Plaridhel
emcees.bio: Plaridhel began his hip-hop journey as an emcee in Tagum's underground scene. He decided to join the 2018 Mindanao Process of Illumination tryouts where he ended up as a special pick. He lost his debut battle against JR Zero, but was quickly able to bounce back with a dominant victory against Placz. His biggest win came at Ahon 12 when he defeated SlockOne in an entertaining battle. Right now, more and more FlipTop fans are starting to recognize Plaridhel's rap ability. The Tagum City representative is armed with intricate wordplays and metaphors which are delivered in a laidback yet still effective manner. Plaridhel also makes music with his group Candelabra. The music video for their song “Biyaya” came out on February 21, 2022.

emcees.name: Plazma
emcees.bio: Plazma started out in the English Conference, giving a solid performance at FlipTop's first Second Sight event. While other emcees rely mostly on bars and jokes, Plazma stays true to his “Horrorcore” style of battling. In every match, the QC-born emcee will come up with different ways of killing you in the most graphic manner. You can see him go full serial killer mode in his Tectonics 2 battle versus USA's Tantrum. His blood-drenched lines became more appreciated when he finally joined the Filipino Conference in 2016. Just a year after his Filipino Conference debut, he participated in the Isabuhay Tournament and reached the finals. Plazma also represents Horrorcore to the fullest in his music. He has released three solo projects, the latest of which is a full-length album entitled "Ang Ulan at ang Delubyo". He is part of the Uprising Records roster.

emcees.name: Poison13
emcees.bio: Poison 13 stood out at the Process of Illumination in Central Luzon, and he improved further when he officially became part of FlipTop's roster. His creative bars and jokes are delivered through impressive multi-syllabic rhymes, making them even more effective. He always comes prepared in his battles, and he has the ability to adapt to whatever style he encounters. When it comes to music, Poison 13 has done a couple of tracks, most of which can be heard online. The music video for his song "Gregor" has now exceeded 1 million views. In November 2021, he and producer JEBeats released their collaboration EP entitled "Lasong Syndrome".

emcees.name: Pricetagg
emcees.bio: Pricetagg's solid lyricism in one of his old tracks impressed the FlipTop staff so much that they decided to give him a battle at the first Zoning event. He took on Badang, and just like his songs, he represented Gangsta Rap to the fullest. After a victorious debut, Pricetagg's winning streak continued. He was officially declared a top tier emcee when he defeated Batas at Ahon 7. Up to now, the La Union-born rapper is still undefeated in 1-on-1 matches. He is well-known not only for his swag, but also for his creative “gun bars” and hard-hitting personals. Whatever firearm you have in mind, he probably has mentioned it already in his battles. Pricetagg aims to continue his success in music. His debut solo album Barcode was released in early 2019, which featured the hit song Kontrabida.

emcees.name: Prince Rhyme
emcees.bio: Prince Rhyme became an official FlipTop battle emcee after an impressive showing at the 2015 Metro Manila Process of Illumination Tryouts. He lost his first four matches then decided to take a break from battle rap in 2017. Four years later, he would return at Zoning 13, beating Makii with his much improved pen game and stronger stage presence. The 3GS member remained consistent since then, scoring victories against Arma, Bagsik, and Vitrum. Fans continue to admire his balance of witty humor and heavy bars. He has also competed in other leagues such as Raplines, Sunugan, and Bahay Katay.

emcees.name: Protege
emcees.bio: At the first-ever Grain Assault event in 2010, Protege quickly established himself as a top-tier emcee in the English Conference. He defeated Fuego in dominating fashion and improved even further from there. Up to now, no one was able to match his impressive flow, intricate multis, and heavy-hitting technical lines. His match versus SinCity is often considered by fans to be his best performance in the league to date. Protege made such a huge impact that he was also invited by King of the Dot (Canada) and 1Outs (Australia) to battle. The QC-based emcee also has a successful career in music. Way before FlipTop started, he and his crew Audible MCs were already rocking shows and dropping dope tracks. The group eventually released their debut album “Undivided Attention” in March of 2006, and it's now regarded as a classic. Protege is currently working on his debut solo project.

emcees.name: Psykadelik
emcees.bio: Psykadelik is part of the legendary Davao group Lifelinez. They are considered one of the frontrunners of leftfield hip-hop in their hometown. Anygma discovered their music in the late 2000s and instantly became a fan. When FlipTop was born, four members of Lifelinez were given spots in the roster, and that includes Psykadelik. His first battle took place at the inaugural Different Ways event, where he was still known as Psycho. He won the match with his trademark unorthodox pen game. Even though he lost his next two battles, he continued to represent his unique brand of hip-hop through music. He has released various solo projects as well as albums with Lifelinez and his collective Kalawakan Krew. Psykadelik also produces beats, which draw inspiration from fellow leftfield artists.

emcees.name: Range
emcees.bio: Range displayed his impeccable freestyle skills at the Ubec Mindfields Tryouts, and despite not reaching the finals, he still became part of FlipTop's roster. Since then, he has been entertaining the crowd not only with his amazing flow, but also with his effective humorous lines. You can see him go all out in his battle with Zeus at the second Gubat event as well as against Damsa at Ahon 9. Even though Range has more losses than wins now, he still continues to be an active battle emcee. After all, giving the people a good show is what really matters. Outside of battle rap, Range also has a successful music career. The music video for his single “RELAX” has now exceed 2.5 million views on YouTube. As for his other tracks, each one has more than 100,000 plays. In January 2022, he finally released his debut solo album "KNBH".

emcees.name: Rapido
emcees.bio: Rapido's first appearance was at Bara Ko, Barako in 2011, where he won against Papew by unanimous decision. His performance was solid indeed, but it was his clash with CrazyMix at Kataga that made him popular among FlipTop fans. At the aforementioned match, he displayed his undeniable skill in speed rapping. Making his flow even more effective are his clever bars and jokes. In 2013, he teamed up with Icaruz at the Dos Por Dos Tournament and even though they lost at the semi-finals, their performance was still met with applause.

emcees.name: Rich Flo
emcees.bio: Rich Flo is one of the special picks at the Process of Illumination 5 tryouts in Central Luzon. His debut battle took place at Aspakan 3, facing fellow FlipTop newcomer EJ Power. He lost the match, but was still able to showcase his confident swag, aggression, and technical abilities. Despite losing his next three battles, Rich Flo didn't stop being an emcee. He took a break from battling to focus on music and emceeing at various clubs. He has released a few solo and collaboration tracks online.

emcees.name: Righteous1
emcees.bio: Not even his disability can stop him from being a dope emcee. Righteous1 debuted at the Sabulong Sumulong event in 2010, wining in dominant fashion against Kahir. He may have more losses than wins now, but his dedication to the scene served as inspiration to the younger generation. While it remains overlooked, his battle versus Asero is undoubtedly his best performance to date. It's where he showcased his technical lines and creative jokes to the fullest. Righteous1 also continues to make an impact in music. His album “Defy Limitations” came out in 2016 and received rave reviews.

emcees.name: Romano
emcees.bio: Hailing from Cabanatuan, Romano instantly won the hearts of fans upon his FlipTop debut. His jokes may be less complex than others, but his aggressive delivery makes them effective. Another notable strength of his is his freestyle skill. Despite forgetting his writtens in his Ahon 5 battle against Makii, he still emerged victorious thanks to his ability to spit off-the-top. Romano proved his top tier status when he became a finalist at the 2015 Isabuhay Tournament and a semi-finalist at the Dos Por Dos with J-King.

emcees.name: Rudic
emcees.bio: Formerly known as Makatang Taga Mindanao, Rudic went to Metro Manila from Pagadian in early 2011 just to participate at the second Process of Illumination tryouts. Despite not reaching the finals, he still became part of the league's official roster after captivating the crowd with his solid lyricism. He made his debut at the Different Ways event in Davao, outrapping Kuscan for three rounds. At Ahon 4, Rudic proved that he's the real deal by defeating the more-experienced Melchrist. His delivery and technical bars improved further when he joined the 2013 Isabuhay Tournament. Even though he lost in the second round against Flict-G, fans were still amazed by his performance. Rudic showcases his skills in music as well. He has released a solo album (“Adik Blues”) and worked with some of the most respected artists in the scene. His most famous track so far is “Suntok”, which features fellow emcees Sunny Bandila, Kintal, and Boca. The music video originally dropped in August of 2014, but was re-uploaded in May 2020. It now has over 13,000 views.

emcees.name: Ruffian
emcees.bio: It didn't take long for Ruffian to catch the attention of FlipTop. He won Floodway Rap Battle League's 1UP Tournament in 2021 and was a finalist at Sunugan sa Kumu in 2022. In 2023, Anygma finally gave him a spot on the league's roster. Ruffian made his debut in Second Sight 11, beating Karisma in what is considered by many as the event's battle of the night. The Rizal emcee continues to shine with his impressive technical lines and raw aggression. When he's not battling, Ruffian focuses on making music. Check out his songs and music videos on his official YouTube channel. You can expect more projects from him in the coming months.

emcees.name: Saint Ice
emcees.bio: Formerly known as Ice Rocks, Saint Ice became part of the FlipTop roster in 2011 after an impressive performance at the finals of the third Process of Illumination. His first official battle took place at the inaugural Zoning event where he took on Lloyd in a hard-hitting English Conference match. 2013 he teamed up with Kris Delano and joined the second Dos Por Dos Tournament. Their battle with Abra and Apekz remains one of the most intense in the league. Saint Ice then went on a hiatus from battling to focus on music and MMA. He made his comeback in 2024, competing at the Won Minutes Luzon event in February. His return to the big stage happened at Zoning 17, where he won against Yuniko. Many appreciated the huge improvements in his technical lyricism, delivery, and overall presence. Saint Ice also stays active in making music.

emcees.name: Sak Maestro
emcees.bio: Sak Maestro may have lost his debut battle against Zero Hour at the inaugural Pakusganay event, but it was the night where people witnessed his one-of-a-kind technical skill. Battle rap fans praised his intricate multis and wordplays as well as his calm but deadly delivery. He continued to showcase his advanced style in his next matches, collecting a few dominant victories along the way. As of now, Sak is the only emcee in FlipTop who has battled in English, Tagalog, and Bisaya. He's also usually the first name that comes to mind when talking about the best in the Mindanao Division. You can hear more of his incredible pen game on his various tracks, which are available online.

emcees.name: Sayadd
emcees.bio: Arguably the most sinister voice in Philippine battle rap, Sayadd quickly made an impact at the very first Process of Illumination. His menacing delivery blends well with his intricate bars and rhyme schemes. He's also renowned for his unpredictable angles, making even the most skilled freestyler struggle to come up with rebuttals. Each battle of his is a must-see, but his clash with Frooz is a good introduction to his unique style. When he's not in the battle arena, Sayadd makes hardcore bangers with his group Illustrado.

emcees.name: Shaboy
emcees.bio: Shaboy didn't become part of the FlipTop roster after his controversial stunt with SirDeo at Ahon 13. As a matter of fact, he already made a name for himself in the underground battle circuit prior to that, competing in leagues such as Motus and PULO. His FlipTop debut took place at Won Minutes Luzon 2024 2, where he defeated Marichu in an entertaining clash. He then proceeded to the big stage at Unibersikulo 12, scoring his second win against Dodong Saypa in another fun bout. From there, he remained active in the league, and is currently undefeated. Apart from his witty and innovative humor, Shaboy can also deliver devastating bars with conviction.

emcees.name: Shehyee
emcees.bio: Shehyee debuted at the first Ahon event and is often regarded as one of the most intense emcees in the league. When you're battling him, you better be prepared to hear plenty of hurtful lines about your professional and personal life. His rhymes are delivered in a very aggressive tone, making them sound even more hard-hitting. He may have more losses than wins, but his 2012 Dos Por Dos championship with Smugglaz and victory against fan favorite Loonie at Ahon 6 were enough to revive his career in battling. In 2018, he silenced all of his doubters by becoming the Isabuhay Champion. Shehyee's success continued in music with his self-titled debut album, which was released in 2013.

emcees.name: Shernan
emcees.bio: Shernan definitely knows how to entertain the crowd. Despite not reaching the finals of Process of Illumination 4, he was still accepted in the league thanks to his brilliant performance. He instantly became famous not only for his mixture of bars and jokes, but also for his creative gimmicks. When he steps on stage, expect Shernan to wear a costume that fits the mood of the battle. His dedication to his craft paid off when he won the Dos Por Dos 3 Championship with M Zhayt. The 2-on-2 battle against Tipsy D and Sinio quickly became the number 1 trend on YouTube upon release.

emcees.name: Sibil
emcees.bio: Sibil officially joined FlipTop's roster after killing it at the Process of Illumination 5 in Metro Manila. He faced Mhot in his debut battle and even though he lost, he was able to showcase his skills in jokes and technical lines. In 2017, he and Dilim teamed up at the 3rd Dos Por Dos, beating Jonas and Lhipkram in the first round. They lost against Damsa and Flict-G in the quarterfinals, but there's no denying that they were able to make an impact in the tournament.

emcees.name: Sickreto
emcees.bio: Sickreto has been battling for over thirteen years now, competing in various underground leagues in Mindanao. He finally made it on the FlipTop stage in 2023 as part of the special picks from Process of Illumination 7. His debut match took place on Pakusganay 7 where took on JP. The crowd instantly admired not only his amazing wordplays, metaphors, and rhyme schemes but also his intense presence. Aside from battling, Sickreto has also enjoyed considerable success in music. Just last year, he won the grand championship at a rap song competition held in Gensan. Make sure you check out his solo and collaboration tracks on his official YouTube channel.

emcees.name: SinCity
emcees.bio: SinCity is undoubtedly one of the emcees who elevated FlipTop's English Conference. In his debut at Down N South, he scored a major upset victory over crowd-favorite Skarm. Viewers immediately got hooked not only to his effective swag but also his straightforward punches. He proved that he wasn't a fluke when he defeated Tim at Sabong Sumulong and NothingElse at Tectonics 1. Apart from battles, SinCity also became well-known for his music. One of his most famous songs is “Let's Get Rich”, which features Loonie. The music video for the track dropped in June of 2014 and now has over 1 million views.

emcees.name: Sinio
emcees.bio: Sinio quickly established himself as FlipTop's “joke king” when he first appeared at Gapo De Gulat 2. Whether it's written or freestyle, his comedic bars always leave a lasting impression. He can also combine his humor with a more serious approach, as seen in his Ahon 7 match against Shehyee. Controversy aside, the aforementioned battle made him a more credible threat in the league. In 2017, he teamed up with Tipsy D for the Dos Por Dos 3 Tournament and they were able to reach the finals. Another notable achievement of Sinio is his clothing line called Real Jokes Clothing. Up to now, his various shirts and caps continue to sell well nationwide.

emcees.name: SirDeo
emcees.bio: SirDeo immediately gained a cult following in the underground battle scene thanks to his blend of theatrics and unorthodox humor. He officially joined the league in 2018 after becoming one of the special picks at the Process of Illumination tryouts. His debut battle took place in March 2019 at the first Won Minutes event, taking on Young One. SirDeo choked on the majority of the match, but fans had a glimpse of his unique style on the first round. 2020 is the year where SirDeo went all out. He redeemed himself from his Won Minutes loss by securing a dominating win against SlockOne. SirDeo continued to showcase his unusual brand of comedy, which quickly made him a household name. He decided to add more serious themes to his rounds in his later battles without abandoning his trademark style. SirDeo has also released various solo tracks online and apart from rap, he's busy working as an educator specializing in ALS (Alternative Learning System).

emcees.name: Sixth Threat
emcees.bio: Sixth Threat became part of the roster after impressing everyone at the Process of Illumination 5 tryouts in Mindanao. He took on Cedie in his debut battle, scoring a 4-1 victory. FlipTop fans instantly got hooked to his complex multisyllabic rhymes as well as his mix of jokes and technical lines. He may have lost the first round of the 2017 Isabuhay, but was able to redeem himself at the 2019 edition of the tournament. Apart from his increased confidence, his pen game also showed huge improvement. He faced Apekz in the finals and became the first emcee from Mindanao to win the championship. Even in music, Sixth Threat continues to be a legitimate threat. He has a group with fellow emcees JR Zero and Jai called 3 Digitz, which instantly gained recognition in the underground scene for their advanced lyricism and flow. In mid 2020, 3 Digitz was officially signed to the legendary label Dongalo Wreckords. Sixth Threat released his solo EP "Thas Business" on the 8th of January 2022.

emcees.name: Skarm
emcees.bio: Skarm immediately made an impact in FlipTop's English Conference when he bodybagged Josh G at the first ever Ahon event. Apart from his remarkable flow, fans were also captivated by his intricate rhyme schemes and brilliant mix of brutal lines and comedy. His most recent battle was against Charron at Tectonics 2 in April 2013, and it's often considered as an underrated gem. Even before the league began, Skarm was already active in the music scene. He was part of AMPON's first compilation album “Dekoding Rhythm”, which dropped in mid 2006. In early 2008, he released his debut solo project entitled “Lazy Boy Blues”. When FlipTop was eventually established, the Pasig-based emcee continued putting out various singles, EPs, and LPs.

emcees.name: SlockOne
emcees.bio: SlockOne began making waves at various underground battle leagues. In 2018, he participated at the Calabarzon Process of Illumination tryouts and ended up as one of the special picks. The Las Pinas-born emcee took on Duma in his debut match at the inaugural Won Minutes event. Despite losing his first encounter, fans still admired his performance. SlockOne then showed vast improvements especially during FlipTop's quarantine battles era. Apart from his freestyle skills, he became renowned for his mesmerizing flow and witty punchlines. SlockOne has his own YouTube channel, which features his music, reactions, and battles from Kumpronta. The aforementioned league aims to give more exposure to up-and-coming local emcees. He also appears on several TEAM PINSAN videos.

emcees.name: Smugglaz
emcees.bio: Smugglaz is already a renowned rapper even before the birth of FlipTop. So when the league was finally established, he instantly became part of the official roster. He made his debut at Down N South in 2010, where he displayed both his rapid fire flow and intricate rhyming style. Some may say that he only says random words in his lines, but he proved them all wrong when he faced Rapido at Bwelta Balentong 3. The Tondo emcee exposed all of his opponent's weaknesses without straying from his trademark style. Many fans called it the biggest bodybag of 2016. Smugglaz also remains active in the music scene. His first solo album “Walking Distance” was released in 2015 under Vertical Brew Music. Since then, he has dropped various singles, most of which became viral.

emcees.name: Snob
emcees.bio: One of the OGs in the league's Mindanao Division, Snob made his debut at the first FlipTop event in Davao. Despite losing the aforementioned match, he continued showing his passion for battle rap. His pen game vastly improved, mixing technical lines with effective jokes and delivering them with utmost confidence. He secured his first victory at 082 Magnitude III, after an entertaining contest with Fukuda. Snob also took part in the 2013 (with Dopee) and 2017 (with Maxford) Dos Por Dos Tournaments. Aside from battling, Snob is active in making songs. He and his group Kalawakan Krew released their debut album “Astral Odyssey” on March 2019. Check it out on their Bandcamp page. Outside of hip-hop, Snob runs a successful clothing shop in his hometown.

emcees.name: Sparo
emcees.bio: Malabon's Sparo made his FlipTop debut at Aspakan on October 6, 2012. He lost against Mocks Wun, but no one can deny the impact of his performance. His next opponents are Thike and Spade, respectively. Despite not getting a W in his three battles, he still gained a solid fanbase due to his hard-hitting lines, strong presence, and incredible speed raps. Even before joining FlipTop, Sparo is already well-known in the underground Pinoy hip-hop scene. His flow is considered one of the best, and he has released several critically-acclaimed albums and singles. He may be inactive in battling for now, but he remains an unstoppable force in music.

emcees.name: Supremo
emcees.bio: Representing Cavite, Supremo first made a name for himself in Motus Battle League, where he was a semifinalist at the Pedestal 2 Tournament. His FlipTop debut took place on May 2024 at Won Minutes Luzon 2. He defeated Philos in a back-and-forth lyrical showcase. Supremo then faced CRhyme at Second Sight 13 and Dave Denver at Zoning 19. Despite failing to get the W, fans still appreciated his performance. Supremo is well-versed in wordplays, metaphors, and multisyllabic rhymes. His aggression also remains highly effective in every match.

emcees.name: Supremo (Mindanao)
emcees.bio: Supremo was one of the standouts at the Process of Illumination 6 tryouts in Mindanao. Despite not winning the championship, his impressive freestyle skills and confidence were enough for him to be included in the special picks. He defeated Scars by unanimous decision in his debut match and remained active since then. His latest battle was a back-and-forth clash with Bonet at Zoning 11. He quickly became renowned for his sharp delivery as well as his hard-hitting technical lines and witty jokes. 2021 was a great year for Supremo because aside from having classic battles and performances in the league, he also released his debut solo album entitled “Bukang Liwayway”. It consists of 13 solo tracks, with production from Tatz Maven, AD Beats, and himself. You can listen to the whole LP on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Sur Henyo
emcees.bio: Sur Henyo was part of the 2015 Process of Illumination in Central Luzon and his impressive showing was enough to get him a spot in FlipTop. He lost his first two battles, but was able to bounce back at the 2017 Isabuhay tournament. His improved pen game and delivery led him to the finals against crowd-favorite Mhot. Despite losing the aforementioned battle, he still managed to get the respect of battle rap fans and fellow emcees. Now, Sur Henyo is well-known not only for his technical bars and confidence but also for his clever angles. The Baguio City representative took a break from battle rap in 2020 to focus on his clothing shop "Bad Crib" as well as his music. Finally, on November 2021, he released his debut solo mixtape entitled "2600 to 4118" The project is now available on YouTube.

emcees.name: Target
emcees.bio: Target has already competed in various freestyle battles way before the league was established. The Paranaque-born emcee decided to give the modern format a try by joining the first ever Second Sight event. He took on Luke and scored a 5-0 victory with ease. At Ahon 1, he faced Dello in what is now considered to be one of the best battles in FlipTop. Target may have lost the aforementioned match, but his performance still made him a top-tier rapper. Since then, he remained active and was able to gain a few notable victories. Apart from his off-the-dome skills, fans also praise his technical bars and aggressive delivery. In October 2010, Target finally released his full-length solo album “It's My Turn Now”. He has worked on various projects with his group DC Clan as well. Right now, he runs a successful YouTube channel, which aside from music, also features reactions and interviews with well-known names in the local hip-hop scene.

emcees.name: Tatz Maven
emcees.bio: Tatz Maven's skill as an emcee and producer was enough for the people behind FlipTop to make him part of the roster. In his debut battle against Dosage, the emcee from GenSan proved that he belongs in the league. Apart from the confidence in his delivery, he also wowed the crowd with his intricate rhyme schemes and metaphors. Fans often claim that his match versus Marshall Bonificaio is the best battle of 2017. Tatz Maven's music career also continues to progress, especially now that he's under Uprising. In 2020, he released his debut album entitled Sige Simula.

emcees.name: Thike
emcees.bio: FlipTop decided to give Thike a shot after watching his impressive 2009 freestyle battle against Damsa on YouTube. The Antipolo-based emcee faced the same opponent in his debut in the league and won by unanimous decision. Fast forward to the present, Thike continues to impress everyone with his hard-hitting punchlines and flawless delivery. You also won't see him choke, thanks to his outstanding freestyling skill. His dedication to Hiphop is more evident through his group No Mannas and the weekly events he organizes in his city.

emcees.name: Tipsy D
emcees.bio: When it comes to “bars”, Tipsy D is one of the first names that come to mind. After impressing the audience at Gapo De Gulat 2, he continued to improve his pen game. His multis, wordplays and metaphors are combined with a confident delivery, thus making him a formidable opponent. What makes him even more threatening is his freestyle ability. He can come up with a well-constructed rebuttal, no matter how strong his opponent's line is. Tipsy D showed his 100 percent in his battle against Sinio at Aspakan 2. He was also a semi finalist at the 2016 Isabuhay Tournament and a finalist at the 2017 Dos Por Dos.

emcees.name: Towpher
emcees.bio: Towpher travelled for over 20 hours from Naga to Calabarzon just to participate at the fifth Process of Illumination tryouts. The long drive didn't stop him from giving a solid performance, which landed him a spot in the league's roster. In his debut battle against Tikboy at Kataga 3, he captivated the crowd with his brilliant combination of serious and humorous bars. Towpher continued to collect impressive wins, the most recent of which was against Marshall Bonifacio at Ahon 10. He and CripLi joined forces at Ahon 7 to take on Lanzeta and Invictus, and were able to score a unanimous decision win. Up to now, fans often refer to the aforementioned match as one of the best battles of 2016. The duo then took part at the 2017 Dos Por Dos Tournamet, and despite losing the first round, they still managed to leave the crowd in awe.

emcees.name: Tulala
emcees.bio: Before FlipTop, Tulala was already active in hip-hop, poetry, and the arts. He was the owner of the legendary venue in Imus called INGAY LIKHA, where many notable events from different genres took place. In battle rap, he first became well-known for his performances in PULO and Tuligsalitaan, of which he is also the founder and president. On February 24, 2024, at Won Minutes Luzon, he made his FlipTop debut, taking on Andros in an entertaining style clash. He got his first win in the league at the next Won Minutes Luzon event by defeating Crispy Fetus. His first main stage battle happened at Second Sight 13. He took on Caytriyu and even though he didn't get the victory, the crowd admired his rounds. Tulala continues to stand out in the scene, thanks to his effective leftfield bars and angles and performance art-style presentation. He remains active in music, releasing a solo album titled "Talaan Ng Walang Nilalaman", several singles, and collaborations with various artists, including his group LU-TANG KLAN.

emcees.name: Tweng
emcees.bio: Tweng may be well-known for using different props in battles, but he's more than that. His unorthodox rhymes and Spoken Word-type delivery also make him truly a one-of-a-kind emcee. The use of props is far from gimmicky, since it's still related to his opponents. Indeed, no one in the league can combine battle rhymes and performance art like him. His performance at the Uprising Royal Rumble is considered by many to be his best yet. As for music, Tweng has released various tracks and a full-length album entitled "Proyekto Sikmahi". He's an active member of Uprising's roster.

emcees.name: Vitrum
emcees.bio: Vitrum started his battling career by competing in various underground leagues in the country. He then joined the Process of Illumination tryouts in 2018 and after a superb performance, became part of the special picks. He debuted at the very first Won Minutes event, taking on Illtimate in an all-out barfest. When the pandemic era began, Vitrum still made sure he stayed active in battle rap. He gained impressive victories against, SirDeo, Bagsik, Onaks, and most recently, Pen Pluma. Apart from his technical rhyming style and very aggressive delivery, Vitrum is also well-known for incorporating socio-political topics in his angles and music. He proved time and time again that he's not afraid to voice out his frustrations with the Philippine government. In 2023, he added relentless dark humor to his style, and the fans loved it. Vitrum then joined the Isabuhay Tournament the year after, where he gave some of his best performances ever. He faced off against GL in the finals and despite failing to win the championship, he still got the respect of the audience and the whole hip-hop scene.

emcees.name: Wrathsol
emcees.bio: Wrathsol started out as a battle emcee in various underground leagues such as WordWar and TIETEST. Anygma eventually saw his matches and immediately gave him a spot in FlipTop's roster. His first bout was against Rich Flo at Kabanata in Nueva Ecija. Wrathsol's intricate rhymes and angles as well as his confident delivery quickly stood out. After losing his next battle against KJap, he decided to take a break from battling to focus on his music. He has released two albums so far, namely “Children of the Future” and “The Majestic Event of the Babylon's Demise”. Let's hope we'll see him again soon in FlipTop!

emcees.name: Yuniko
emcees.bio: Representing Caloocan City, Yuniko first emerged in the league as a participant at the 2018 Metro Manila Process of Illumination. His impeccable freestyle skills were enough to make him the champion. He faced off against Lil Weng at Won Minutes, winning via unanimous decision. Since then, Yuniko continues to enthral fans not only with his complex wordplays and multis, but also his clear delivery. When he's not verbally crushing his opponents, Yuniko is killing it in the studio. He has released a few solo and collaboration tracks, all of which can be heard on his YouTube channel. The music video for his latest track “Simula” is out now!

emcees.name: Zaito
emcees.bio: Even before the league started, Zaito is already regarded one of the best freestylers in the Philippines. He was so impressive on the mic that FlipTop invited him to its first Ahon event. Despite losing against Loonie, Zaito still received plenty of praise for his entertaining off-the-top rhymes. He then started to adjust to the modern format of battling and eventually became a fan favorite. Up to now, his unique humor never fails to make the viewers laugh out loud. He can also mix his comedic punches with effective serious bars, as seen in his classic “subtitle” battle against KOTD's Charron. Zaito's talent is further displayed in his debut album “Ganti Ng Patay”, which was released in 2015 under Uprising.

emcees.name: Zaki
emcees.bio: Formerly known as RNSM, Zaki first made his presence known in the underground battle scene. He quickly became well-known when he joined Sunugan's tournament in 2021 and reached the finals by beating top names such as M Zhayt, Romano, and Lhipkram. His performance was enough for Anygma to give him a spot at the league's roster. Zaki's debut match took place at Ahon 12, which is FlipTop's biggest event of the year. He faced Don Pao in a highly-acclaimed back-and-forth battle. Zaki is renowned not only for his brilliant wordplays and angles, but also for his intensity in his delivery. His aggression makes every punchline much more effective. When he's not battling, Zaki focuses on making music. You can check out his tracks and music videos on his YouTube channel.

emcees.name: Zend Luke
emcees.bio: Zend Luke quickly became one of the Mindanao Division's most recognized names thanks to his very impressive Filipino vocabulary and relentless aggression. He first made waves at the 2018 Process of Illumination tryouts event, where he ended up in the special picks of the night. Zend Luke's first official battle took place on Pakusganay 5, facing off against N-Flowinz. He scored a 5-0 win, which is indeed very impressive especially for an up-and-comer. Not even COVID-19 could halt the momentum of Zend Luke. Despite the pandemic, the CDO-based emcee continued his battle rap journey. His most notable victory so far was against Harlem at the quarterfinals of the 2021 Isabuhay Tournament. Fans and emcees often regard that match as one of the best style clashes ever. Zend Luke wasn't able to reach the finals of Isabuhay, but there's no doubt that his leftfield lyricism has left a mark. He has also released two EPs, namely “Alegorya” and “Pag-Ibig”, both of which can be heard on YouTube.

emcees.name: Zero Hour
emcees.bio: Already a legend in the Davao underground hip-hop scene, Zero Hour made his FlipTop debut in 2012 at Different Ways 2. He lost against Aklas but his intricate lyricism and spoken word-type delivery still caught the attention of battle rap fans. A few months later, he returned with a much-improved pen game and a more commanding presence, leading to a dominating win against Tweng. The Davao lyricist then faced off against Sak Maestro in Pakusganay. It is often regarded as one of the best battles in the league. He went on to beat other top names such as Sayadd and Apoc. Zero Hour is a member of the rap group Down Loud Crew. They've released three albums so far, all of which received critical acclaim for their uncompromising, raw style of hip-hop. Zero Hour is currently working on new music, so watch out!
